descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Eclipse Jetty. The HTTP/1.1 parser is vulnerable to request smuggling when chunk extensions are used. An attacker can inject crafted requests to manipulate and trick the parser. This issue can lead to security controls bypass, cache poisoning or unauthorized endpoint access.

descriptions.description: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

cna.title: HTTP Request Smuggling via Chunked Extension Quoted-String Parsing

descriptions.value:
In Eclipse Jetty, the HTTP/1.1 parser is vulnerable to request smuggling when chunk extensions are used, similar to the "funky chunks" techniques outlined here:
  *  https://w4ke.info/2025/06/18/funky-chunks.html

  *  https://w4ke.info/2025/10/29/funky-chunks-2.html


Jetty terminates chunk extension parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings instead of treating this as an error.




POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

1;ext="val
X
0

GET /smuggled HTTP/1.1
...





Note how the chunk extension does not close the double quotes, and it is able to inject a smuggled request.

cna.title: Micca KE700 Acceptance of previously used rolling codes

descriptions.value: CAPEC-395: Bypassing Electronic Locks and Access Controls

solutions.value:
*  Enforce strict anti-replay: The receiver must maintain a persistent state (e.g., the counter value of the last valid code). It must never accept a code with a counter value less than or equal to the last known valid counter.

  *  Secure resynchronization logic: The logic triggered by an old code is the flaw and must be removed. Secure resynchronization should only be triggered by codes that are ahead of the current counter to allow a "drifted" key fob to re-sync.

supportingMedia.value:

descriptions.value: The Greenshift – animation and page builder blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 12.8.3. This is due to missing authorization and post status validation in the `gspb_el_reusable_load()` AJAX handler. The handler accepts an arbitrary `post_id` parameter and renders the content of any `wp_block` post without checking `current_user_can('read_post', $post_id)` or verifying the post status. descriptions.value:

This direct control can enable unauthorized access to internal network resources or services that would typically be inaccessible from external networks.

cna.title: Advanced Custom Fields: Extended <= 0.9.2.7 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Data Exposure via Multiple AJAX Endpoints

descriptions.value: The Advanced Custom Fields: Extended plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized access of data and triggering of server-side actions in all versions up to, and including, 0.9.2.7. This is due to multiple AJAX handlers registered for unauthenticated users (`wp_ajax_nopriv_*`) that fail to implement proper `current_user_can()` authorization checks. While these handlers use ACF's `acf_verify_ajax()` function to validate cryptographic nonces, the `acf_nonce` values are generated for guest users and publicly exposed in the page source of any frontend page utilizing an ACF form. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the guest nonce and bypass WordPress visibility permissions, leading to the unauthorized disclosure of post titles and internal Flexible Content layout structures. The vulnerability was partially patched in version 0.9.2.4.

cna.title: Heap buffer overflow in session parsing with wolfSSL_d2i_SSL_SESSION() function

descriptions.value: CAPEC-100 Overflow Buffers

A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability exists in wolfSSL's wolfSSL_d2i_SSL_SESSION() function. When deserializing session data with SESSION_CERTS enabled, certificate and session id lengths are read from an untrusted input without bounds validation, allowing an attacker to overflow fixed-size buffers and corrupt heap memory. A maliciously crafted session would need to be loaded from an external source to trigger this vulnerability. Internal sessions were not vulnerable.

cna.title: Quiz and Survey Master (QSM) <= 10.3.5 - Authenticated (Contributor+) SQL Injection via 'merged_question' Parameter

affected.product: Quiz and Survey Master (QSM) – Easy Quiz and Survey Maker

descriptions.value: The Quiz and Survey Master (QSM) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'merged_question' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 10.3.5. This is due to insufficient sanitization of user-supplied input before being used in a SQL query. The sanitize_text_field() function applied to the merged_question parameter does not prevent SQL metacharacters like ), OR, AND, and # from being included in the value, which is then directly concatenated into a SQL IN() clause without using $wpdb->prepare() or casting values to integers. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

descriptions.value:
Emails sent by pretix can utilize placeholders that will be filled with customer data. For example, when {name}
 is used in an email template, it will  be replaced with the buyer's 
name for the final email. This mechanism contained a security-relevant bug:

It was possible to exfiltrate information about the pretix system through specially crafted placeholder names such as {{event.__init__.__code__.co_filename}}.
 This way, an attacker with the ability to control email templates 
(usually every user of the pretix backend) could retrieve sensitive 
information from the system configuration, including even database 
passwords or API keys. pretix does include mechanisms to prevent the usage of such 
malicious placeholders, however due to a mistake in the code, they were 
not fully effective for this plugin.

Out of caution, we recommend that you rotate all passwords and API keys contained in your pretix.cfg file.

cna.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in mlflow/mlflow

descriptions.value: A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in MLflow versions prior to 3.9.0. The `_create_webhook()` function in `mlflow/server/handlers.py` accepts a user-controlled `url` parameter without validation, and the `_send_webhook_request()` function in `mlflow/webhooks/delivery.py` sends HTTP POST requests to this attacker-controlled URL. This allows an authenticated attacker to force the MLflow backend to send HTTP requests to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary external servers. The lack of input sanitization, URL scheme filtering, or allowlist validation on the webhook URL enables exploitation, potentially leading to cloud credential theft, internal network access, and data exfiltration.

cna.title: Hostinger Reach <= 1.3.8 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Integration API Key Update

affected.product: Hostinger Reach – AI-Powered Email Marketing for WordPress

descriptions.value: The Hostinger Reach – AI-Powered Email Marketing for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data due to a missing capability check on the 'handle_ajax_action' function in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to use the 'hostinger_reach_connection_notice_action' action to update the API key value stored in the database. cna.title: Login No Captcha reCAPTCHA <= 1.8.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via PHP_SELF

descriptions.value: The Login No Captcha reCAPTCHA plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the `$_SERVER['PHP_SELF']` superglobal in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.0. This is due to the `authenticate()` function storing the unsanitized output of `basename($_SERVER['PHP_SELF'])` in the `login_nocaptcha_error` WordPress option when a login attempt is made from a non-standard login page (e.g., xmlrpc.php). The `admin_notices()` function then echoes this stored value directly into the admin dashboard HTML without escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts that execute when an administrator with a whitelisted IP address visits the WordPress dashboard within 30 seconds of the attack.

cna.title: Libsoup: libsoup: http request smuggling via duplicate content-length headers

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Cavid for reporting this issue.

descriptions.value: A request smuggling vulnerability exists in libsoup's HTTP/1 header parsing logic. The soup_message_headers_append_common() function in libsoup/soup-message-headers.c unconditionally appends each header value without validating for duplicate or conflicting Content-Length fields. This allows an attacker to send HTTP requests containing multiple Content-Length headers with differing values.

descriptions.value:
The affected product accepts user-supplied input within a URL parameter without enforcing expected sanitization or encoding before rendering it within the response. This condition allows for the injection of malicious JavaScript payloads.

cna.title: Cache poisoning via insecure-by-default cache key

solutions.value: We strongly recommend Pingora users to upgrade to Pingora v0.8.0 or higher

supportingMedia.value: We strongly recommend Pingora users to upgrade to Pingora v0.8.0 or higher

workarounds.value: Pingora users on previous versions may also remove any of their default CacheKey usage and implement their own that should at minimum include the host header / authority and upstream peer’s HTTP scheme.

supportingMedia.value: Pingora users on previous versions may also remove any of their default CacheKey usage and implement their own that should at minimum include the host header / authority and upstream peer’s HTTP scheme.

descriptions.value:
A cache poisoning vulnerability has been found in the Pingora HTTP proxy framework’s default cache key construction. The issue occurs because the default HTTP cache key implementation generates cache keys using only the URI path, excluding critical factors such as the host header (authority). Operators relying on the default are vulnerable to cache poisoning, and cross-origin responses may be improperly served to users.


Impact

This vulnerability affects users of Pingora's alpha proxy caching feature who relied on the default CacheKey implementation. An attacker could exploit this for:

  *  Cross-tenant data leakage: In multi-tenant deployments, poison the cache so that users from one tenant receive cached responses from another tenant


  *  Cache poisoning attacks: Serve malicious content to legitimate users by poisoning shared cache entries




Cloudflare's CDN infrastructure was not affected by this vulnerability, as Cloudflare's default cache key implementation uses multiple factors to prevent cache key poisoning and never made use of the previously provided default.


Mitigation:

We strongly recommend Pingora users to upgrade to Pingora v0.8.0 or higher, which removes the insecure default cache key implementation. Users must now explicitly implement their own callback that includes appropriate factors such as Host header, origin server HTTP scheme, and other attributes their cache should vary on.


Pingora users on previous versions may also remove any of their default CacheKey usage and implement their own that should at minimum include the host header / authority and upstream peer’s HTTP scheme.

cna.title: Unauthorized session creation via reserved framework path access

descriptions.value: CAPEC-554 Functionality Bypass

solutions.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

supportingMedia.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

descriptions.value:
An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in Vaadin 14.0.0 through 14.14.0, 23.0.0 through 23.6.6, 24.0.0 through 24.9.7 and 25.0.0 through 25.0.1, applications using Spring Security due to inconsistent path pattern matching of reserved framework paths.

Accessing the /VAADIN endpoint without a trailing slash bypasses security filters, and allowing unauthenticated users to trigger framework initialization and create sessions without proper authorization.

Users of affected versions using Spring Security should upgrade as follows: 14.0.0-14.14.0 upgrade to 14.14.1, 23.0.0-23.6.6 to 23.6.7, 24.0.0 - 24.9.7 to 24.9.8, and 25.0.0-25.0.1 upgrade to 25.0.2 or newer.

Please note that Vaadin versions 10-13 and 15-22 are no longer supported and you should update either to the latest 14, 23, 24, 25 version.

Accessing the /VAADIN endpoint without a trailing slash bypasses security filters, and allowing unauthenticated users to trigger framework initialization and create sessions without proper authorization.

cna.title: Pagelayer <= 2.0.9 - Incorrect Authorization to Authenticated (Contributor+) Mail Relay Configuration via 'contacts'

affected.product: Page Builder: Pagelayer – Drag and Drop website builder

descriptions.value: The Page Builder: Pagelayer – Drag and Drop website builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Incorrect Authorization in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.9. This is due to the pagelayer_save_content AJAX handler allowing users with basic post-edit capability to persist pagelayer_contact_templates metadata on posts they can edit (including pending posts), while the unauthenticated pagelayer_contact_submit endpoint later consumes that metadata by user-controlled post/form identifiers without enforcing a privileged or published-context boundary. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to configure arbitrary contact-form mail templates that are usable through unauthenticated form submission via the contacts parameter. In typical deployments this template feature is configured via Pagelayer Pro UI; however, the vulnerable backend trust path is still present. This issue may be chained with CVE-2026-2442 to increase exploitability and attacker control over outbound email behavior.

cna.title: lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`

descriptions.value: The _.unset and _.omit functions in Lodash are vulnerable to prototype pollution. The fix for CVE-2025-13465 only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as Object.prototype, Number.prototype, and String.prototype. The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior. The issue is patched from 4.18.0 to 4.18.1 depending on the package: lodash, lodash-es, and lodash-amd in 4.18.1, and the standalone lodash.unset and lodash.omit packages in 4.18.0.

cna.title: AddFunc Head & Footer Code <= 2.3 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Custom Fields

descriptions.value: The AddFunc Head & Footer Code plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the `aFhfc_head_code`, `aFhfc_body_code`, and `aFhfc_footer_code` post meta values in all versions up to, and including, 2.3. This is due to the plugin outputting these meta values without any sanitization or escaping. While the plugin restricts its own metabox and save handler to administrators via `current_user_can('manage_options')`, it does not use `register_meta()` with an `auth_callback` to protect these meta keys. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts via the WordPress Custom Fields interface that execute when an administrator previews or views the post.

source.value: Dmitry "InfoSecDJ" Janushkevich of Trend Micro Zero Day Initiative

descriptions.value:
Socomec DIRIS A-40 HTTP API Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of Socomec DIRIS A-40 power monitoring devices. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

descriptions.value: The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.7 via deserialization of untrusted input in the 'download_csv' function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. descriptions.value: The Livemesh Addons for Beaver Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the `[labb_pricing_item]` shortcode's `title` and `value` attributes in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. Specifically, the plugin uses `htmlspecialchars_decode()` after `wp_kses_post()`, which decodes HTML entities back into executable code after sanitization has occurred. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

cna.title: Formidable Forms <= 6.28 - Unauthenticated Payment Amount Manipulation via 'item_meta' Parameter

affected.product: Formidable Forms – Contact Form Plugin, Survey, Quiz, Payment, Calculator Form & Custom Form Builder

descriptions.value: The Formidable Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to an authorization bypass through user-controlled key in all versions up to, and including, 6.28. This is due to the `frm_strp_amount` AJAX handler (`update_intent_ajax`) overwriting the global `$_POST` data with attacker-controlled JSON input and then using those values to recalculate payment amounts via field shortcode resolution in `generate_false_entry()`. The handler relies on a nonce that is publicly exposed in the page's JavaScript (`frm_stripe_vars.nonce`), which provides CSRF protection but not authorization. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to manipulate PaymentIntent amounts before payment completion on forms using dynamic pricing with field shortcodes, effectively paying a reduced amount for goods or services.

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cna.title: App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight <= 5.5.10 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'role' Parameter

affected.product: App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight

descriptions.value: The App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.10. This is due to the `verify_role()` function in `AuthTrails.php` explicitly whitelisting the `wcfm_vendor` role alongside `subscriber` and `customer`, and assigning it directly via `wp_insert_user()` without integrating with WCFM Marketplace's vendor approval workflow. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register an account with the `wcfm_vendor` role by supplying the `role` parameter in the `/wp-json/app-builder/v1/register` REST API endpoint, bypassing the standard WCFM vendor approval process and immediately gaining vendor-level privileges (product management, order access, store management) on sites where WCFM Marketplace is active.

descriptions.value: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability was identified in the server-side template rendering mechanism used by the Glassfish gadget handler. The application processes .xml files and evaluates user-supplied values within a context where Expression Language (EL) “expressions” are processed without proper sanitization or escaping. cna.title: WP Mail Logging <= 1.15.0 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via Email Log Message Field

descriptions.value: The WP Mail Logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 1.15.0 via deserialization of untrusted input from the email log message field. This is due to the `BaseModel` class constructor calling `maybe_unserialize()` on all properties retrieved from the database without validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object by submitting a double-serialized payload through any public-facing form that sends email (e.g., Contact Form 7). When the email is logged and subsequently viewed by an administrator, the malicious payload is deserialized into an arbitrary PHP object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present.

cna.title: Concierge::Sessions versions from 0.8.1 before 0.8.5 for Perl generate insecure session ids

descriptions.value: CAPEC-115 Authentication Bypass

solutions.value: Upgrade to Concierge::Sessions v0.8.5 or later.

descriptions.value:
Concierge::Sessions versions from 0.8.1 before 0.8.5 for Perl generate insecure session ids. The generate_session_id function in Concierge::Sessions::Base defaults to using the uuidgen command to generate a UUID, with a fallback to using Perl's built-in rand function. Neither of these methods are secure, and attackers are able to guess session_ids that can grant them access to systems. Specifically,

  *  There is no warning when uuidgen fails. The software can be quietly using the fallback rand() function with no warnings if the command fails for any reason.
  *  The uuidgen command will generate a time-based UUID if the system does not have a high-quality random number source, because the call does not explicitly specify the --random option. Note that the system time is shared in HTTP responses.
  *  UUIDs are identifiers whose mere possession grants access, as per RFC 9562.
  *  The output of the built-in rand() function is predictable and unsuitable for security applications.

cna.title: Libslirp: libslirp: out-of-bounds heap read in icmp_forward_error() leading to information disclosure

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Piyusha Akash (Manifold Operations) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Red Hat is not aware of a practical temporary workaround that fully mitigates this issue or meets Red Hat Product Security's standards for usability, deployment, applicability, or stability. Customers are advised to apply the relevant security updates when/if they become available.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-04) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to clamp quoted IPv4 payload length to actual buffer bounds in libslirp icmp_forward_error before copying data into ICMP error responses: upgrade to the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds, which clamp s_ip_len to the source buffer length msrc->m_len before copying payload data into the ICMP error packet, closing crafted truncated IPv4 packets with ip_len exceeding mbuf length. Until patched, this is a concern on guests or containers transmitting network traffic through libslirp, so restrict untrusted guests or containers from transmitting network traffic across libslirp virtual network interfaces. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying out-of-bounds heap read defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libslirp in icmp_forward_error(). When building an ICMP error response, the length of the quoted original IPv4 packet was taken from the IP header without clamping it to the actual buffer length. A truncated or malformed packet could cause an out-of-bounds heap read, leaking host memory into the ICMP error packet returned to a guest or container.

cna.title: Wiki.js: Stored XSS via Vue Slot Directives in Page Content

descriptions.value: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated user with write:pages can store JavaScript expressions in the v-slot:tabs or v-slot:content attributes of page HTML because server/modules/rendering/html-security/renderer.js adds those executable Vue directives to DOMPurify's allowlist. The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

cna.title: psqlODBC stack buffer overflow when quoting long schema and table names

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. identifierEscape bounds every write to the output buffer, including the closing quote and the terminator.

workarounds.value: Do not pass SQL text from untrusted sources to the driver.

descriptions.value: When psqlODBC quotes a schema or table name into a 128-byte stack buffer, its length check lets it write up to two bytes past the end of the buffer for a long name. The names come from the application's SQL text: the table of a statement the driver parses to describe its columns, and the target of the last INSERT when the driver rewrites SELECT @@IDENTITY. In the @@IDENTITY rewrite, a column name sent by the server can also write one byte past the buffer. The bytes written past the buffer are a double quote and a NUL. An application that forwards untrusted SQL text to the driver exposes its process to stack corruption. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in the Vaadin Rich Text Editor via an Unescaped Video Embed

descriptions.value: CAPEC-592 Stored XSS

solutions.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

supportingMedia.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

workarounds.value: Persist the editor content through the default HTML value, set and read with setValue and getValue, which is sanitized on the server, rather than through asDelta(). An application that must use asDelta() should strip video inserts from the delta before storing or replaying it.

descriptions.value:
The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode.

Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

cna.title: Beta9 build sandbox escape via chroot-only isolation

scenarios.value: Default clip v2 layered image build on a privileged build-pool worker

timeline.value: Fix merged in pull request 1897 (commit a28bf12)
Fixed release worker-0.1.756 published. No vendor security advisory was filed with the pull request.

solutions.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. That release drops chroot isolation: Buildah RUN steps use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant build arguments are applied inside the build container rather than in the Buildah process environment. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15. Gateway 0.1.776 is the gateway tag cut from the same commit; the isolation change itself is in the worker image.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. That release drops chroot isolation: Buildah RUN steps use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant build arguments are applied inside the build container rather than in the Buildah process environment. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15. Gateway 0.1.776 is the gateway tag cut from the same commit; the isolation change itself is in the worker image.

references.name: Handle sandbox edge cases (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: Beta9 turns each shell command in a tenant image definition into a Dockerfile RUN line and executes it with Buildah on the build worker. The worker image sets BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot, and no buildah invocation passes --isolation, so the step only changes its filesystem root. It keeps the worker pod's PID, network, IPC, and user namespaces, runs as uid 0, and holds CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. PID 1 in that procfs is the worker entrypoint, so /proc/1/root is the worker container's filesystem and is writable. That filesystem contains the runc, buildah, and runsc binaries the worker uses to start tenant containers, the worker's Kubernetes service account token, and the host directories mounted into the pod. Worker pods are privileged. Clip v2 layered builds are the default, so a tenant with a workspace token reaches this by submitting one image build. The read-only proof confirmed the shared namespaces, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, and that the worker's runc binary is visible at /proc/1/root. Fixed in worker 0.1.756: Buildah RUN steps, including the WORKDIR mkdir, use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant ARG values are passed only into the build container.

Reaching this condition depends on a specific, application-chosen way of requesting several result rows at once.

cna.title: Apache Axis2/Java: XML External Entity (XXE) injection via imported WSDL/XSD documents

descriptions.value: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. When a client built an AxisService from a WSDL URL, through ServiceClient or AxisService.createClientSideAxisService, wsdl4j import resolution was enabled and the documents named by wsdl:import and xsd:import were parsed by wsdl4j's own XML parser, which processes DOCTYPE declarations and external entities. An attacker who controls a WSDL, or a document it imports, could therefore read local files or make the JVM issue network requests. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: MotoPress Appointment Booking <= 2.4.8 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Customer Name via /customers/create REST Endpoint

descriptions.value: The MotoPress Appointment Booking Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.4.8 via the public '/motopress/appointment/v1/customers/create' REST endpoint. The route is registered with permission_callback => '__return_true' and the handler's 'name' parameter is not sanitized before being written to the custom wp_mpa_customers table via $wpdb->insert, nor is it escaped on output in the admin bookings list when the viewing user lacks the 'mpa_edit_customer' capability (such as the plugin-defined Appointment Employee role). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

cna.title: psqlODBC does not validate column numbers and row indexes in binding and descriptor functions

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. SQLBindCol rejects column numbers above 32767 with SQLSTATE 07009, a negative descriptor count is ignored, and the column and row indexes are range-checked.

workarounds.value: Validate column numbers (1..32767 and within the result set) and row numbers (within the rowset) in the application before calling the driver.

descriptions.value: Several psqlODBC entry points use an application-supplied column number or row index as an array index without validating it. SQLBindCol with a column number above 32767 wraps the binding count negative and a later copy runs off the array. A negative SQL_DESC_COUNT on an application row descriptor unbinds columns at negative indexes. SQLColAttribute with a very large column number uses a negative index. SQLSetPos(SQL_ADD) does not check the row number against the rowset size. An application that forwards untrusted column or row numbers exposes its process to out-of-bounds reads and writes. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

descriptions.description: CWE-129 Improper Validation of Array Index

cna.title: Use-After-Free in MongoDB Server JavaScript Support for Aggregation Leads to Information Disclosure

descriptions.value: A use-after-free weakness in MongoDB Server's server-side JavaScript support for aggregation may allow a stale reference to previously freed process memory to be read and returned. An authenticated user with minimal or no assigned roles can trigger this condition over the normal network protocol by submitting a single crafted aggregation request, with no additional privileges or non-default configuration. Successful triggering this issue may result in adjacent process memory contents being returned, including data that undermines memory-layout randomization, and may in some cases affect server availability.

cna.title: CGI versions from 4.62 before 5.00 for Perl allow cross-site scripting via a raw apostrophe in URLs returned by url and self_url

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

descriptions.value:
CGI versions from 4.62 before 5.00 for Perl allow cross-site scripting via a raw apostrophe in URLs returned by url and self_url.

Both pass the URL through URI's canonical method, which leaves an apostrophe in the path raw and decodes the %27 that query parameter escaping produces, so an apostrophe in the request path or a parameter appears raw in the result.

An application that places the URL in a single-quoted HTML attribute or JavaScript string is open to cross-site scripting.

The application retrieves configuration data over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing an attacker capable of manipulating network traffic to replace legitimate server responses with malicious configurations. cna.title: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow memory, CPU and disk exhaustion via missing or unenforced request size, parameter and upload limits

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

workarounds.value: For deployments that cannot upgrade, limit the request body size at the web server and set $CGI::POST_MAX.

descriptions.value:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow memory, CPU and disk exhaustion via missing or unenforced request size, parameter and upload limits.

$CGI::POST_MAX defaults to no limit, and when set is not enforced for chunked multipart bodies or for the boundary line of a multipart body without a boundary= parameter. Bodies saved as PUTDATA, POSTDATA or PATCHDATA uploads are read into memory in one go, and nothing limits the number of parameters or uploads.

cna.title: AMP for WP <= 1.1.19 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content

affected.product: AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages

descriptions.value: The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.19 via comment content rendered on AMP post pages. The plugin registers an output-buffer callback ampforwp_the_content_filter_full() on the 'wp' action (priority 999) that applies a set of tag-agnostic and quote-agnostic regular expressions — notably /onclick=[^>]*/ — to the entire AMP page output after approved comments have already been echoed into it; these regexes do not understand HTML tag or attribute-value boundaries, so a kses-legal comment that places strings like 'onclick="' inside a title attribute value can trigger deletion of the title's closing quote, causing the browser to re-parse what was previously textual content inside the attribute value as live HTML attributes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, after an administrator has approved the comment.

cna.title: Easy Digital Downloads <= 3.7.2 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Administrator Account Takeover via Guest Checkout Email Binding at PayPal Capture

affected.product: Easy Digital Downloads – eCommerce Payments and Subscriptions made easy

descriptions.value: The Easy Digital Downloads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authentication bypass leading to administrator account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 3.7.2. During a PayPal guest checkout, the email address entered in the guest-checkout field is trusted as proof of identity: edd_get_purchase_form_user() binds the new guest order to an existing WordPress user purely on an email-address match, rewriting the order's user_id to that user's ID. The PayPal capture sink PurchaseUser::maybe_log_in_after_capture() then looked the user up by the order email (get_user_by( 'email', $order->email )) and, when $order->user_id equalled that user's ID (which the email-binding step guarantees), issued an authenticated session with wp_set_auth_cookie(). An unauthenticated attacker who starts a guest checkout using an administrator's email address (where that administrator has no existing EDD customer record) and completes the PayPal purchase flow therefore receives an authenticated session as that administrator — a full account takeover. The same sink is reachable through the standard PayPal checkout and the REST UnbrandedCard and Fastlane flows.

cna.title: Prefab UI Pyodide sandbox escape to host RCE

scenarios.value: FastMCP server with GenerativeUI enabled, Deno installed, and no authentication configured
Authenticated client allowed to call tools on a server that executes untrusted code in the Generative UI sandbox

timeline.value: Pyodide sandbox added with --allow-read, --allow-write, and --allow-net (commit fc4362f3, pull request 334)
prefab-ui 0.14.0 published on PyPI, the first release that includes the sandbox
prefab-ui 0.20.2 published. This is the release confirmed in testing.
Reported to PrefectHQ as GHSA-595q-jv4r-q7j9. The advisory is still in triage and has no CVE id.
Fix merged in pull request 538 (commit 030f074). The runner revokes read, write, and network permission before accepting code.
prefab-ui 0.21.0 published on PyPI with the fix. No vendor advisory text was published with the release.

references.name: Refresh dependencies and fix renderer and sandbox regressions (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: Prefab UI's Generative UI sandbox runs caller-supplied Python inside Pyodide, Python compiled to WebAssembly, in a Deno subprocess. The feature is documented as isolation for untrusted code, including LLM-written UI. From prefab-ui 0.14.0 through 0.20.2 the launcher starts Deno with unrestricted --allow-read, --allow-write, and --allow-net, and the runner leaves the Deno API on the JavaScript global object. Pyodide's js module proxies that global, so the Python can call Deno.readTextFileSync and Deno.writeTextFileSync. A caller who can supply the code can read and write files as the server OS user, and can persist code execution by writing a .pth file into the server virtualenv's site-packages. The usual remote path is FastMCP's GenerativeUI provider, which registers the MCP tool generate_prefab_ui and forwards that tool's code argument into this sandbox. On a FastMCP server with no authentication configured, any client who can reach the server can call the tool. With authentication, any client allowed to call tools can. Generative UI is opt-in, and the host must have Deno installed. Confirmed on prefab-ui 0.20.2. Fixed in 0.21.0: after the runtime and Prefab sources load, the runner revokes Deno read, write, and network permission before it accepts code, the process is started with --no-prompt so a permission request cannot grant them again, and bootstrap network access is limited to cdn.jsdelivr.net. The fix is commit 030f074 (pull request 538).

This issue only affects MongoDB processes running on macOS with the Apple SecureTransport TLS provider.

cna.title: Unescaped Download File Name Allows Content-Disposition Parameter Injection in Vaadin Flow

descriptions.value: CAPEC-554 Functionality Bypass

solutions.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

supportingMedia.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

workarounds.value: Escape or reject double quotes, backslashes and control characters in any file name that does not come from the application itself before passing it to DownloadEvent.setFileName or DownloadEvent.inline.

descriptions.value:
DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="<name>" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 24.8.0 - 24.8.17
Vaadin 24.9.0 - 24.9.25
Vaadin 24.10.0 - 24.10.13
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 24.9.26 or newer
Upgrade to 24.9.26
Upgrade to 24.10.14
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

Vaadin versions below 24.8 are not affected: the DownloadEvent API does not exist in them.

cna.title: An improper TLS certificate validation vulnerability exists in the ADM online update service

credits.value: Jincheng Wang (@winmt) from Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

descriptions.value: CAPEC-157 Sniffing Attacks

An improper TLS certificate validation vulnerability exists in the ADM online update service. An unauthenticated attacker capable of performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack against the device's firmware update connection can impersonate the update server using an untrusted TLS certificate and supply malicious update metadata. The attacker may cause a crafted firmware image to be installed and execute arbitrary code with root privileges when automatic firmware updates are enabled.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

cna.title: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow form fields to be smuggled past proxies and WAFs via multipart parsing that differs from the RFCs

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

descriptions.value:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow form fields to be smuggled past proxies and WAFs via multipart parsing that differs from the RFCs.

The multipart/form-data parser matches the boundary anywhere rather than at the start of a line, uses the boundary without its leading -- for some client-supplied User-Agent values, finds the Content-Disposition name and filename inside the quoted values of other parameters, and corrupts parts when the boundary nears the 4096-byte read size.

cna.title: Stop Spammers Classic <= 2026.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'author' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Stop Spammers Classic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' POST parameter in versions up to, and including, 2026.6. An unauthenticated POST handled on init stores the attacker-supplied author field (after sanitize_text_field, which does not escape single quotes) into the ss_stop_sp_reg_stats option history. The Log Report admin page then renders that stored value inside a single-quoted JavaScript string within a double-quoted onclick attribute using esc_js(); because esc_js() uses _wp_specialchars with ENT_COMPAT it does not escape single quotes, allowing the stored value to break out of the JS string literal and inject arbitrary JavaScript. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute whenever an administrator with manage_options access clicks the 'Report to SFS' link on an attacker-poisoned log row (the StopForumSpam API key must be configured for that link to be rendered — the field is empty by default). Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

cna.title: Search Everything <= 8.1.9 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Sensitive Information Exposure via 's' Parameter via search_everything AJAX Action

descriptions.value: The Search Everything plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 via the search_everything AJAX action. The handler registered at `wp_ajax_search_everything` performs no capability check, no ownership check, and no nonce verification before running a WP_Query over `$_GET['s']` and returning the raw WP_Post objects — including the `post_password` field — as JSON. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to extract cleartext passwords for every password-protected post on the site and, when the plugin's draft/attachment/metadata search options are enabled by an administrator, to read draft and pending post contents they otherwise have no capability to view.

cna.title: Heap Buffer Over-read via Non-Terminated Link Data in H5L__extern_traverse

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in H5L__extern_traverse() in src/H5Lexternal.c, the default traversal callback for external links. The callback locates the target file name and object path within the link’s user data using strlen() without validating the buffer against its stored size (udata_size, which was marked unused). A crafted HDF5 file containing an external link whose data is not NULL-terminated, or is too short to hold both strings, causes strlen() to read past the end of the udata heap buffer, and the derived object path pointer may also point outside the buffer. The overrun is unbounded and continues until a zero byte is found. The flaw is triggered when the malicious link is traversed, for example when opening an object through it. An attacker who can get a user or application to access a crafted file can cause a denial of service, and adjacent heap contents may be incorporated into the external file name or object path the library attempts to open.

cna.title: Admin Columns <= 7.1.7 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'User-Agent' Header via comment_agent

descriptions.value: The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The kses sanitization pass in classes/Sanitize/Kses.php uses wp_kses_allowed_html('post') augmented with iframe[src] and the data: protocol; because wp_kses_attr_check accepts any data-* attribute on any allowed tag without inspecting its value, a payload embedded inside a data-ac-tip attribute survives intact and is subsequently assigned to innerHTML by assets/js/table.js, bypassing the apparent mitigation entirely.

cna.title: Authorization bypass via redirected FLE2 state-collection writes in encrypted CRUD path

descriptions.value: In MongoDB Server, an authenticated user with insert privileges on a collection could craft a command with specially constructed encryption-related parameters to redirect internal Queryable Encryption metadata writes to metadata belonging to other encrypted collections within the same database. The server’s authorization layer validated only the user-facing target collection namespace, while subsequent internal writes derived from client-supplied parameters were performed with elevated internal privileges, bypassing the original caller’s permission scope. This could allow unauthorized writes into another collection’s Queryable Encryption metadata, potentially corrupting encrypted index state and compaction operations.

cna.title: Privilege escalation via fail-open user lookup in X.509 cluster-membership guard

descriptions.value: A flaw in MongoDB’s X.509 cluster-membership authentication guard could allow a holder of a cluster-member certificate to gain elevated internal privileges when a specific deployment configuration is in use. An internal check, which prevents a certificate recognized as a cluster member from also being treated as a regular user, does not correctly distinguish between certain error conditions encountered during user lookup. Under certain timing conditions, this can cause the check to be bypassed, granting the connection full internal system privileges. Triggering this issue requires possession of a valid cluster-member TLS certificate, non-default X.509 cluster authentication configuration, and specific conditions during the user cache lookup process.

descriptions.value:
Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an organization member who is removed or given a lower role to keep acting at their old role through anything they had open at the time. The dashboard reads the member's role once when a page mounts, in the assign_org_to_scope hook of NervesHubWeb.Auth, and the console, local shell and device event stream channels check membership once at join. Removing a member or changing their role tells none of them, so open pages keep carrying out actions and open consoles keep running commands on the device until the page reloads or the socket disconnects.

The dashboard also opens consoles over NervesHubWeb.UserSocket with a token that holds only the user's id, is accepted for 24 hours, and is not revoked by signing out, which disconnects only the session's LiveViews. Whoever holds a token taken from a page can open consoles as that user, within the user's current membership, until it expires.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an organization member who is removed or given a lower role to keep acting at their old role through anything they had open at the time. The dashboard reads the member's role once when a page mounts, in the assign_org_to_scope hook of NervesHubWeb.Auth, and the console, local shell and device event stream channels check membership once at join. Removing a member or changing their role tells none of them, so open pages keep carrying out actions and open consoles keep running commands on the device until the page reloads or the socket disconnects.

The dashboard also opens consoles over NervesHubWeb.UserSocket with a token that holds only the user's id, is accepted for 24 hours, and is not revoked by signing out, which disconnects only the session's LiveViews. Whoever holds a token taken from a page can open consoles as that user, within the user's current membership, until it expires.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

descriptions.value:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated organization member with the view role to change devices and deployment groups via LiveView events reserved for the manage role. The event handlers that add and delete device certificates, add and remove tags, overwrite or clear a device's manual location, remove a device from its deployment group, move matched devices into a deployment group or remove unmatched ones, import devices from a CSV, and start, retry or delete firmware delta builds carry out the change without calling authorized!/2, and the pages render the controls to every member.

A view member can add a certificate that lets whoever holds its key connect as the device, delete a certificate so the device can no longer authenticate with it, and change which deployment group, and so which firmware release, a device receives. Everything stays within the organizations the member belongs to.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
The dashboard reads the member's role into current_scope when a page mounts, and each privileged event handler is expected to call authorized!/2 with the permission it needs, all of which resolve to the manage role in lib/nerves_hub_web/helpers/authorization.ex. These handlers never do:

Device settings tab (NervesHubWeb.Components.DevicePage.SettingsTab): hooked_event/3 for delete-certificate, and handle_progress/3 for the certificate upload, which should require device:update.

Device details tab (NervesHubWeb.Components.DevicePage.DetailsTab): hooked_event/3 for add-tag, remove-tag, save-location-changes and clear-manual-location-information (device:update), and remove-from-deployment-group (device:set-deployment-group).

Deployment group page (NervesHubWeb.Live.DeploymentGroups.Show and NervesHubWeb.Components.DeploymentGroupPage.Summary): handle_event/3 for move-matched-devices-to-deployment-group and remove-unmatched-devices-from-deployment-group, and handle_progress/3 for the device_csv upload (device:set-deployment-group), plus generate-firmware-deltas, retry_delta and delete_delta (deployment_group:update).

The pages show every one of these controls to view members, so each change takes a click, and a client can send the events directly over the LiveView socket regardless.

cna.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption in MongoDB Server Aggregation Framework via Internal Expression Leads to Denial of Service

descriptions.value: An issue in MongoDB server’s aggregation framework allows an authenticated user with read privileges to cause a denial of service by sending specially crafted aggregate commands using an internal expression. Despite its internal naming, this expression is registered as accessible to any authenticated client. By supplying crafted input parameters across multiple concurrent connections, each evaluation triggers unbounded memory allocations with no per-expression memory limits enforced. This can exhaust available server memory and cause the mongod process to be terminated by the operating system’s out-of-memory killer.

cna.title: NULL Pointer Dereference in H5HL_unprotect via Corrupted File

descriptions.value: CAPEC-153 Input Data Manipulation

HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in H5HL_unprotect() in src/H5HL.c. H5HL_protect() pins a single metadata cache entry for a local heap, either the heap prefix or the separate data block, and H5HL_unprotect() unpins it on the final unprotect. When the metadata cache destroys a corrupted local heap entry, H5HL__prfx_dest() unlinks it from the heap by setting heap->prfx or heap->dblk to NULL. A crafted HDF5 file can therefore reach H5HL_unprotect() with no cached object to unpin, and the function passes the NULL pointer to H5AC_unpin_entry(). This causes an assertion failure in debug builds and a NULL pointer dereference and crash in release builds. An attacker who can get a user or application to open and traverse a malicious file can cause a denial of service.

cna.title: Heap Buffer Over-read via Malformed Message Size in HDF5's H5O__chunk_deserialize

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in H5O__chunk_deserialize() in src/H5Ocache.c. When decoding object header messages, the declared message size is checked against the end of the chunk image before the remainder of the message header (flags, and for version 2 object headers, the optional creation index) has been decoded. Because the message body begins after these fields, a message can start up to four bytes further into the chunk than the size check accounts for. A crafted HDF5 file can declare a message size that passes the check but extends past the end of the chunk image, causing the message’s decode callback, for example H5O__mtime_new_decode() in src/H5Omtime.c, to read beyond the heap allocation. The flaw is reachable during H5Fopen() on a crafted file. An attacker who can get a user or application to open a malicious file can cause a denial of service or limited disclosure of process memory.

cna.title: Uncontrolled Recursion in HDF5 H5B__iterate_helper() via Crafted File

descriptions.value: HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in H5B__iterate_helper() in src/H5B.c. When iterating a version 1 B-tree, the function does not verify that a child node’s level matches the expected level. That check is performed only in H5B__cache_deserialize() when a node is first loaded into the metadata cache. A crafted HDF5 file whose B-tree child pointer refers back to a node already in the cache, such as a node that points to itself, bypasses the check and causes unbounded recursion, leading to stack exhaustion and a crash. This can be triggered by calling H5Gget_info() or H5Gget_num_objs() on a group in the crafted file, which reaches H5B_iterate() through H5G__obj_info() and H5G__stab_count(). An attacker who can get a user or application to open a malicious file can cause a denial of service.

cna.title: MongoDB SBE $locf Window Accumulator Use-After-Free Enables Heap OOB Read and Server Crash

descriptions.value: A use-after-free issue exists in MongoDB’s SBE (Slot-Based Execution) implementation of a window function accumulator used by certain $setWindowFields aggregation pipelines. Under specific conditions, the accumulator can retain a dangling pointer to memory that has since been freed. When this stale pointer is later dereferenced during serialization of the carried-forward value, it can result in a heap out-of-bounds read that may expose adjacent heap contents and crash the mongod server. An authenticated user with readWrite privileges on a database can trigger this issue by crafting a specific aggregation pipeline.

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

descriptions.value:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow an infinite loop on a short request body when $DISABLE_UPLOADS is set.

When $CGI::PUTDATA_UPLOAD or an upload hook is set, read_postdata_putdata takes a request body that is not a form submission. With $CGI::DISABLE_UPLOADS set, it discards the body by reading until Content-Length bytes have arrived. Once a body shorter than its Content-Length runs out, every read returns 0, so the loop never ends.

A client can keep a server process spinning with one such request.

cna.title: Beta9 host filesystem exposure via volume path traversal

scenarios.value: Tenant with a workspace token deploying a function that attaches a volume

timeline.value: Confirmed affected releases worker-0.1.745 and gateway-0.1.769 are current
Fix merged in pull request 1897 (commit a28bf12)
Fixed releases worker-0.1.756 and gateway-0.1.776 published. No vendor security advisory was filed with the pull request.

solutions.value: Upgrade the gateway to 0.1.776 or later and the worker to 0.1.756 or later. Volume identifiers and mount paths are rejected when they are empty, ".", "..", or contain a slash (identifiers) or a ".." segment (mount paths). The gateway also refuses a volume the workspace does not own. Stubs stored before the check existed are validated when they are launched. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released on 2026-09-15.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade the gateway to 0.1.776 or later and the worker to 0.1.756 or later. Volume identifiers and mount paths are rejected when they are empty, ".", "..", or contain a slash (identifiers) or a ".." segment (mount paths). The gateway also refuses a volume the workspace does not own. Stubs stored before the check existed are validated when they are launched. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released on 2026-09-15.

references.name: Handle sandbox edge cases (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: A Beta9 tenant can attach a volume when deploying a function, endpoint, or task queue. The gateway builds the host path by joining the shared volumes root, the workspace name, and the volume identifier from the stub configuration. Nothing checks that the identifier names a volume that workspace owns. Parent-directory segments in the identifier collapse the joined path to the worker's filesystem root, and the worker bind-mounts that path into the sandbox read-write unless the volume was explicitly marked read-only. A tenant with a workspace token can therefore read and write the worker's files, including other tenants' volumes stored on that machine. Confirmed against gateway 0.1.769 and worker 0.1.745. Fixed in gateway 0.1.776 and worker 0.1.756: volume identifiers and mount paths are validated before a mount is built, including for stubs saved before the check existed, and the gateway rejects a volume that does not exist or is not owned by the workspace.

cna.title: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow HTTP header injection via entity decoding after the newline check in header and unchecked values in multipart_start and do_push

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

descriptions.value:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow HTTP header injection via entity decoding after the newline check in header and unchecked values in multipart_start and do_push.

With autoEscape off, header decodes HTML entities in extra header values after its newline check, so an encoded CR or LF reaches the response. multipart_start does not check header values for newlines, and do_push does not check the type it prints in each part.

An application that passes request data into these header values can be made to add headers or split the response.

cna.title: Beta9 container escape via unvalidated sandbox file paths

scenarios.value: Tenant with a workspace token and a running sandbox on a worker that serves the sandbox file API

timeline.value: Fix merged in pull request 1897 (commit a28bf12)
Fixed release worker-0.1.756 published. No vendor security advisory was filed with the pull request.

solutions.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. Sandbox file APIs and workspace sync use os.OpenRoot, so parent-directory segments and symbolic links stay inside the container root or the mount source. File operations refuse read-only mounts and do not write through a symlink swapped in after path resolution. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. references.name: Handle sandbox edge cases (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: The Beta9 worker serves the sandbox file API from outside the container. getHostPathFromContainerPath turns the tenant's container path into a worker path. If the unresolved path starts with a mount destination, including the default upload mount at /tmp/.beta9, the remainder is joined onto that mount's source with filepath.Join, which cleans parent-directory segments after the prefix check. A long enough run of those segments names any absolute path on the worker. A path that matches no mount is joined onto the container root and opened in the worker's own filesystem, so an absolute symbolic link such as /var/run pointing at /run is followed against the worker root. Upload, download, stat, list, find-in-files, replace-in-files, and delete-file all call this helper. A tenant with a workspace token and one running sandbox can read, write, list, and delete files on the hosting worker as root, including files of other tenants on that machine. A read-only proof downloaded the worker pod's Kubernetes service account token through the file API for a path that did not exist inside the sandbox. In the shipped remote-node manifests that service account is bound to cluster-admin. Fixed in worker 0.1.756: sandbox file operations and workspace sync open paths with os.OpenRoot, so parent-directory and symlink lookups stay inside the container root or the mount source.

cna.title: fastify vulnerable to Denial of Service via uncaught exception on handlerTimeout with streaming responses

descriptions.value: fastify is a web framework for Node.js. In versions 5.8.0 through 5.12.7, when the server is configured with a nonzero handlerTimeout and a route returns a streaming response, a request whose stream has already sent its headers but stays open past the timeout crashes the server. When the timeout fires, Fastify tries to send a new error response on a response that has already started, raising an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT that terminates the Node.js process and interrupts any other in-flight requests. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a single request to an affected streaming endpoint, so the impact is availability only, and exploitation requires the non-default handlerTimeout to be set. The default handlerTimeout of 0 is not affected. The issue is fixed in fastify 5.12.8, and users should upgrade to 5.12.8 or later. As a workaround, set handlerTimeout to 0, which disables the affected timeout path.

workarounds.value: Leave Debug and CommLog disabled in production. If logging is needed, set Logdir in the driver's section of odbcinst.ini (PostgreSQL Unicode or PostgreSQL ANSI) to a directory writable only by the user running the application.

cna.title: frr: bgpd Send Hold Timer expiry bypasses the FSM, leaving a phantom Established session or crashing bgpd with Graceful Restart

credits.value: Srinivasan Koona Lokabiraman <srinivasan@nexthop.ai> (not reported as security issue)

workarounds.value: No configuration workaround fully prevents the issue. Monitor bgpd logs for "has not made any SendQ progress for 2 holdtimes" and run "clear bgp <neighbor>" for the affected neighbor, which raises a real FSM event and recovers the peer (this does not prevent the abort when Graceful Restart was negotiated, if the restart timer fires first).

descriptions.value: In FRRouting, bgpd does not correctly close a BGP session when the Send Hold Timer (RFC 9687) expires, i.e. when a neighbor has stopped accepting data from the router for twice the hold time. The connection is closed, but bgpd still considers the session to be up. A BGP neighbor that keeps sending KEEPALIVEs but stops reading from its connection, at a time when the router has a large amount of data to send to it (for example while sending it a full routing table), can trigger this. If the neighbor announced Graceful Restart support, bgpd crashes shortly after the session is closed, taking down all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat this each time bgpd restarts. Otherwise, the session stays stuck in the Established state: the neighbor's routes stay installed and keep being advertised to other peers, and the neighbor cannot reconnect until an operator clears the session manually. The neighbor does not need to be malicious; an overloaded or stuck peer can trigger the same behavior. No special configuration is required: any established BGP neighbor can trigger the issue, and Graceful Restart helper mode, which leads to the crash, is enabled by default.

descriptions.description: CWE-372 Incomplete Internal State Distinction: Send Hold Timer expiry tears down the connection outside the BGP FSM, leaving it in the Established state without a socket

cna.title: undici vulnerable to cross-origin credential disclosure via array-of-tuples headers bypassing redirect stripping

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, the redirect interceptor strips sensitive headers such as Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, and Host when a request is redirected to a different origin, but when request headers are supplied as an array of name and value tuples (a valid documented input, for example from Object.entries), the redirect handler misreads them as a flat list so the header names never match and the sensitive headers are not removed. If a header-normalizing interceptor such as cache or deduplicate is composed outside the redirect interceptor, it then serializes the retained headers onto the cross-origin request, disclosing the caller's origin-bound credentials to the unrelated redirect destination. This is a representation-dependent bypass of the cross-origin header stripping added in CVE-2024-30260. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, supply request headers as a plain object or a flat name and value array rather than an array of tuples, or compose the redirect interceptor outside the normalizing interceptor.

In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, the redirect interceptor strips sensitive headers such as Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, and Host when a request is redirected to a different origin, but when request headers are supplied as an array of name and value tuples (a valid documented input, for example from Object.entries), the redirect handler misreads them as a flat list so the header names never match and the sensitive headers are not removed. If a header-normalizing interceptor such as cache or deduplicate is composed outside the redirect interceptor, it then serializes the retained headers onto the cross-origin request, disclosing the caller's origin-bound credentials to the unrelated redirect destination. This is a representation-dependent bypass of the cross-origin header stripping added in CVE-2024-30260. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, supply request headers as a plain object or a flat name and value array rather than an array of tuples, or compose the redirect interceptor outside the normalizing interceptor.

cna.title: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow the POSTDATA, PUTDATA, PATCHDATA and XForms:Model parameters to be set from the query string or form fields

solutions.value: Upgrade to CGI 5.00 or later.

workarounds.value: For deployments that cannot upgrade, check the request Content-Type before trusting param('POSTDATA').

descriptions.value:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow the POSTDATA, PUTDATA, PATCHDATA and XForms:Model parameters to be set from the query string or form fields.

CGI stores a non-form request body under POSTDATA, PUTDATA or PATCHDATA, and an XForms body under XForms:Model, but also accepts these names from the query string, a form field or a multipart part, so an application cannot tell a client-sent value from the real body.

A cross-site HTML form can post POSTDATA={"admin":true} to an endpoint that reads JSON from param('POSTDATA'), a request forgery that needs no CORS preflight.

cna.title: Eclipse Ditto gateway accepts `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` from a URL query parameter, allowing unauthenticated subject impersonation (default Helm chart)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-115 Authentication Bypass
CAPEC-151 Identity Spoofing

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

cna.title: Temporal Server Kubernetes compute provider builds a client from caller-supplied configuration and runs a caller-chosen command on the Worker Service host

descriptions.value: Command execution on the host running the Temporal Worker Service, as the operating system account the server process runs under, reachable from an ordinary namespace read role. That process holds the persistence credentials for every namespace in the cluster as well as the cluster's TLS material, so the effect is cross-namespace and cluster-wide rather than confined to the caller's own namespace. In the official container image the server runs as an unprivileged account rather than root, which bounds host takeover but does not bound access to the credentials and key material the server process itself holds.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Temporal Server 1.32.2 or 1.31.5. Both remove the k8s compute provider from default builds, so it is no longer compiled into the official binaries and container images, and both require a namespace write role for ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig. Operators who cannot upgrade immediately can apply the workaround below, which closes the same path without waiting for a release. The 1.30 release line does not depend on the Worker Controller Instance module at all and is unaffected. Note that the fixed releases remove the provider from default builds and do not change where its Kubernetes client configuration comes from: an operator who builds Temporal Server with the k8s compute provider included and permits it in the allowlist still accepts that configuration from the caller's request.

workarounds.value: Remove k8s from the dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled, at the global level and in every namespace-constrained override. On Temporal Server 1.31.0 through 1.31.2, also set the setting to an explicit list naming only the compute providers the deployment intends to permit, omitting k8s, because leaving it unset permits every registered provider; an explicit empty list denies every compute provider. The request is then rejected with InvalidArgument before the provider runs. This is dynamic configuration, so it takes effect without restarting the server and is available during an incident rather than only at a maintenance window. Deployments that use a custom authorizer can additionally require namespace write access for ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig, which removes the read-role route but not the write-role route.
