descriptions.value: Temporal Server compiles a Worker Controller Instance module, go.temporal.io/auto-scaled-workers, into its Worker Service, and that module registers a compute provider named k8s whose function is to manage workers running in a Kubernetes cluster. The k8s provider built its Kubernetes client from the client configuration supplied in the caller's request rather than from operator configuration, and building and using that client could run a command of the caller's choosing on the Worker Service host, under the account the server process runs as. Two frontend operations reach the provider. CreateWorkerDeploymentVersion requires a namespace write role. ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig is registered as a read-only namespace operation, so an authenticated caller holding only a read role in a single namespace can reach the provider through it, and that route does not require a worker deployment to already exist. Execution happens while the submitted configuration is validated, so no scaling decision, task arrival, or unusual request sequence is required. Because the Worker Service process holds the persistence credentials for every namespace in the cluster and the cluster's TLS material, the consequence reaches beyond the caller's namespace to the cluster as a whole. The provider is present in the official temporal-server binaries and container images for the affected releases. The control that keeps it unreachable is the compute provider allowlist, the dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled. On Temporal Server 1.31.0 through 1.31.2 that allowlist does not deny by default: when the setting is unset the check is skipped and every registered compute provider is permitted, k8s included, so a stock deployment of those releases is exposed. On 1.31.3 and later 1.31 releases, and on 1.32.0 and later 1.32 releases, the allowlist denies by default, and a deployment is exposed only where k8s has been added to it. The 1.30 release line does not include the Worker Controller Instance module and is unaffected. To determine whether a deployment is affected, check the following together. The deployed Temporal Server version is in an affected range. The Worker Service is running, which it is in the default service set and therefore in a stock deployment. The effective value of workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled contains k8s, or, on 1.31.0 through 1.31.2 only, is unset; check both the global value and every namespace-constrained override, because an override can add k8s for a single namespace. And authorization is configured, meaning a real authorizer and claim mapper are in place; a deployment running with no authorizer already grants every caller unrestricted access to every namespace, so it has no namespace boundary for this to cross. Deployments that use a custom authorizer should also check whether it permits ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig to callers without namespace write access. The separate per-namespace dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.enabled does not gate the affected path on any affected release.

CWE-749: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
CWE-1188: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default

configurations.value: Exploitation requires all of the following at once. The deployment runs an affected Temporal Server release with the Worker Service enabled, which is the default service set, so a stock deployment satisfies this. The k8s compute provider is permitted by the dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled, either globally or for the caller's namespace. On 1.31.0 through 1.31.2 an unset value permits every registered provider, so no operator action is needed there; on 1.31.3 and later 1.31 releases and on 1.32 releases, the operator must have added k8s to the list. Authorization is configured through an authorizer and a claim mapper; without it every caller already holds unrestricted access to every namespace and there is no namespace boundary to cross. The caller holds a read role in some namespace, which is what the frontend requires to validate a worker deployment version's compute configuration, or a write role, which is what it requires to create a worker deployment version. cna.title: @fastify/cors vulnerable to Denial of Service on a CORS preflight with the onSend hook

descriptions.value: @fastify/cors is the CORS plugin for the Fastify web framework. In versions 8.2.0 through 11.3.x, an application that registers the plugin with the non-default onSend hook option crashes on a CORS preflight. On an OPTIONS request that carries the Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method headers, the plugin calls reply.send from inside the onSend hook and re-enters the send pipeline, so a second write of the response headers throws an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT that can terminate the Node.js process when no process-level handler is installed. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a single preflight request, so the impact is availability only, and exploitation requires the non-default onSend configuration. The issue is fixed in @fastify/cors 11.4.0, where onSend is no longer an accepted hook value and registration fails with a clear error instead of crashing at request time, and users should upgrade to 11.4.0 or later. As a workaround, use any other hook such as the default onRequest, or set preflight to false.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing.

In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable.

This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. What the limit counts. Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 subtracts the result of headers_size/1 from the remaining :length limit. headers_size/1 sums byte_size(key) + byte_size(value) for each header. The part delimiter, the colon and CRLF of each header line, and the blank line that ends the header block are not counted.

2. Inputs that cost zero. A part without headers has an empty header list, so its charge is 0. A header line that holds only : followed by CRLF also costs 0, because :plug_multipart.parse_hd_name/3 accepts the empty name and returns the header {"", ""}.

3. Retention. multipart_type/1 returns {:binary, nil} for a part without a content-disposition header. The parser then prepends {nil, headers, body} to its accumulator for that part. Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.multipart_to_params/3 drops these entries, but only after the whole request body is read.

4. Limits that stay in effect. Plug.Conn.read_part_headers/2 limits one header block to the smaller of :length and :read_length. No limit applies to the sum over all parts.

On plug 1.20.3 with length: 100_000, a 4.5 MB body of 500,001 parts without headers parsed successfully with a peak of 92 MiB in the parser process. A 4.5 MB body of 50 parts with 30,000 : header lines each peaked at 283 MiB.

cna.title: psqlODBC ODBC escape parser stack buffer overflow

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The argument offset array is initialized and bounded, and the escape body copy reserves room for the terminator.

workarounds.value: Do not pass SQL text from untrusted sources to the driver, or reject text containing ODBC escape sequences ({fn ...}, {d ...}, {t ...}, {ts ...}, {escape ...}) before it reaches the driver.

descriptions.value: The psqlODBC parser for ODBC escape sequences in application SQL text writes the argument offsets of a {fn} escape into a fixed 16-entry stack array without a bound and does not initialize the array. An escape with too many arguments overflows the stack, and a reference to an unsupplied argument copies arbitrary bytes into the query. The copy of a {d}, {t}, {ts}, or {escape} body also writes one byte past a 128-byte stack buffer. An application that forwards untrusted SQL text to the driver exposes its process to memory corruption. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Restrictions for BuddyPress <= 1.5.4 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Request URI String Interpolation in eval()

descriptions.value: The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). Because PHP interpolates double-quoted strings, a payload of the form {${...}} in the URL path is executed during interpolation, so no quote breakout is required and WordPress' slashing does not mitigate it. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server with a single GET request. The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled exception in cache-interceptor response replay

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when the cache interceptor is composed with a downstream handler that throws during response processing (such as the built-in dump interceptor exceeding its maxSize, or the decompress interceptor rejecting more than five Content-Encoding values), a throw raised asynchronously while a cached response is replayed escapes as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminates the Node.js process. A malicious or compromised HTTP server can crash any such client by serving a cacheable response that triggers the throw on replay, including on a 304 revalidation of a stale entry, so the impact is availability only. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, avoid composing the cache interceptor with a response handler that throws during response processing until upgrading.

affected.product: SEOPress – AI SEO Plugin & On-site SEO

descriptions.value: The SEOPress – AI SEO Plugin & On-site SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'seopress_google_analytics_affiliate_tracking' and 'seopress_google_analytics_download_tracking' settings in versions up to, and including, 10.3. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on these settings as they are interpolated into the inline Google Analytics tracking snippet by seopress_google_analytics_js(): the affiliate value receives no sanitization at all (it is omitted from inc/admin/sanitize/Sanitize.php) and lands inside a <script> block, while the download value is only passed through sanitize_text_field() and lands inside a JavaScript regular-expression literal that preserves parentheses, semicolons and slashes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above (where an administrator has delegated the SEOPress 'analytics' capability under Settings > Advanced > Security — the precondition Wordfence accepted for CVE-2026-101357), to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

psqlODBC uses a server-supplied column name as a format string

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. Each percent sign in the server-supplied column name is doubled before the name is placed in the format string.

workarounds.value: Set UpdatableCursors=0 in the connection string or DSN, or use read-only cursors (SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY).

descriptions.value: For an updatable cursor over a table without OIDs that has an auto-increment int4 column, psqlODBC places that column's name, as reported by the server, into a printf-style format string. It later expands that string with one argument while it builds the WHERE clause of its positioned SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements. A column name that contains format directives makes the driver read unrelated memory, which can crash the application or copy client memory into query text sent to the server. The name can come from a server not trusted under current SSL settings, or from any database user who can create a table that the application reads with an updatable cursor. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Silent element-count truncation via 32-bit bit-length overflow in packed-bit vector views

descriptions.value: A weakness in the BSON library's handling of a specialized binary vector data type allows an arithmetic wraparound when computing the number of elements described by an oversized attacker-supplied value. On builds where the platform word size is 32 bits, an application that parses untrusted BSON data can be made to process only a small fraction of the supplied elements while the operation reports success, producing results that disagree with byte-oriented accessors and with 64-bit builds of the same library. No authentication or user interaction is required beyond getting the application to parse the data. The impact is limited to data integrity; memory safety is not affected and no information is disclosed.

cna.title: psqlODBC does not escape a server-supplied column name in its updatable-cursor queries

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The driver doubles each double quote in the stored column name, and does not use a name that does not fit its buffers to identify rows.

workarounds.value: Set UpdatableCursors=0 in the connection string or DSN, or use read-only cursors (SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY).

descriptions.value: For an updatable cursor over a table without OIDs that has an auto-increment int4 column, psqlODBC uses that column to identify rows. It places the column's name, as reported by the server, between double quotes in its keyset queries and in the WHERE clause of its positioned SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements, without doubling any double quote in the name. A column name that contains a double quote therefore changes the SQL that the driver runs with the application's privileges, including which rows a positioned UPDATE or DELETE affects. Any database user who can create a table that the application reads with an updatable cursor can choose such a name, and so can a server not trusted under current SSL settings. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

references.name: Users with the ‘view’ role in an organization can move devices into it

descriptions.value:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter.

A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
As a user with manage in organization A and view in organization B, where B has an active deployment group:

* On A's devices page, give a device you control the tags B's deployment group asks for. A view member can see the group's conditions.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Target selection. The bulk actions sidebar (NervesHubWeb.Components.BulkActionsSidebar) lists the products of every organization in current_scope.user.orgs. Choosing one sends target-product to NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index, which requires device:update in the current organization and then calls NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2. That query joins the product's organization to its org_users rows and filters on the user's id only, so any membership in the target organization satisfies it, including the view role.

2. The move. move-devices-product passes the selected devices, or every device matching the current filter, to NervesHub.Devices.BulkActions.move_many/3, which calls Devices.move/3 for each one and rewrites its org_id and product_id. No check of the user's role in the target organization happens on this path, while the API's move in NervesHubWeb.API.DeviceController requires manage there.

3. Effect. The moved device still authenticates with its own certificate. On its next connection it is matched against the target product's deployment groups by platform, architecture and tags, joins one, and is sent that group's firmware with a download URL.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Parse Server before 8.6.109 and 9.0.0 before 9.10.6-alpha.1 Information Disclosure via Object Update Response

descriptions.value: Parse Server before 8.6.109 and 9.0.0 before 9.10.6-alpha.1 returns stored field values in object update responses without checking read access, so clients whose class-level permissions or object ACLs allow update but not read can see object data. Attackers can update such objects to read atomic operation results (Increment, Add, AddUnique, Remove), Cloud Code trigger-set values, and, for dot notation keys under certain conditions, the whole stored parent field.

cna.title: MongoDB C Driver leaks the decompressed reply buffer when an OP_COMPRESSED reply fails to parse (denial of service)

descriptions.value: A memory management flaw in the MongoDB C Driver's handling of compressed responses may cause the client library to hold on to memory that is never released. An unauthenticated party that controls the database endpoint a client application connects to may cause repeated, unbounded memory growth in that application, which may result in the application becoming unavailable. No credentials, transport security settings, or user interaction are required.

cna.title: Mass assignment of organization, product and deployment group IDs allows users to write into other organizations and receive their firmware

descriptions.value: Any user who manages devices in an organization of their own can attach their device to another organization's deployment group and receive its firmware, move devices into that organization's product, add firmware signing keys and products to it, and have a certificate authority provision devices into its product. Devices that already belong to the other organization are not controlled, and no firmware can be uploaded to it.

solutions.value: The fixed release's migration takes every device off a deployment group that belongs to a different product and logs each one. Upgrading undoes nothing else done this way. After upgrading, check the database for devices whose organization does not own their product, for signing keys in org_keys whose created_by_id has never been a member of the key's organization, and for certificate authorities whose JITP product belongs to another organization, and remove what you do not recognize. A device moved wholly into another organization, and a product added to one, leave nothing that sets them apart, so review your organization's devices and products as well.

descriptions.value:
Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one.

A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
As an admin of organization A, with organization B having an active deployment group whose current release is firmware B:

* POST /api/orgs/<A>/products/<A's product>/devices with {"identifier": "planted", "deployment_id": <B's deployment group ID>}. The device is created in A, on B's deployment group.
* Create a device key for it, then connect it, reporting the platform and architecture of firmware B. When the deployment runs, the device is sent an update for firmware B with its download URL.
* To move a device instead, PUT /api/orgs/<A>/products/<A's product>/devices/<identifier> with {"org_id": <B's ID>, "product_id": <B's product ID>}. The response is 201, and the device is now in B's product.

  2. Create a device key for it, then connect it, reporting the platform and architecture of firmware B. When the deployment runs, the device is sent an update for firmware B with its download URL.
  3. To move a device instead, PUT /api/orgs/<A>/products/<A's product>/devices/<identifier> with {"org_id": <B's ID>, "product_id": <B's product ID>}. The response is 201, and the device is now in B's product.

1. `POST /api/orgs/<A>/products/<A's product>/devices` with `{"identifier": "planted", "deployment_id": <B's deployment group ID>}`. The device is created in A, on B's deployment group.
2. Create a device key for it, then connect it, reporting the platform and architecture of firmware B. When the deployment runs, the device is sent an update for firmware B with its download URL.
3. To move a device instead, `PUT /api/orgs/<A>/products/<A's product>/devices/<identifier>` with `{"org_id": <B's ID>, "product_id": <B's product ID>}`. The response is `201`, and the device is now in B's product.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Device API and device forms. NervesHubWeb.API.DeviceController.create/2 sets org_id and product_id from the route, then hands the rest of the request to Device.changeset/2; update/2 hands the whole request over. The changeset casts org_id, product_id, deployment_id, deleted_at and the server-managed update state, so an update can move the device into another organization's product and either request can place it on another organization's deployment group. The device settings form in NervesHubWeb.Components.DevicePage.SettingsTab and the new device form in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.New reach the same changeset with the same effect.

2. Signing key and product forms. NervesHubWeb.Live.Org.SigningKeys and NervesHubWeb.Live.Products.New build their parameters with Enum.into(submitted, %{"org_id" => session_org_id}), so a submitted org_id overrides the session's, and the key or product is created in the organization named by the client.

3. JITP settings. NervesHub.Devices.CACertificate.JITP.changeset/2 casts any product_id, through the API and the dashboard, so devices the certificate authority provisions are created in another organization's product.

4. Firmware delivery. When a planted device connects, NervesHub.ManagedDeployments checks its deployment group membership by firmware version, platform and architecture only, all reported by the device, so it stays on the foreign group and is sent that group's current release with a download URL.

cna.title: RSS Aggregator by Feedzy <= 5.2.13 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Feed Item Title

affected.product: RSS Aggregator by Feedzy – Feed to Post, Autoblogging, News & YouTube Video Feeds Aggregator

descriptions.value: The RSS Aggregator by Feedzy – Feed to Post, Autoblogging, News & YouTube Video Feeds Aggregator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'item_title (parsed from feed <item><title>)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have previously configured a Feed-to-Post import pointing at an attacker-controlled feed URL, after which the attacker can rotate payloads at will without any further interaction with the site.

cna.title: Missing Authorization Check in MongoDB Server Replication-Related Administrative Command Leads to Unauthorized Data Access

descriptions.value: MongoDB Server may omit an authorization check on the resource that a replication-related administrative command actually targets, because that check is conditioned on a value taken from the client's own request. A user holding backup and restore privileges may therefore read and relocate collections outside the set that user is permitted to access. This may result in unintended access to data and unintended changes to the collection catalog.

descriptions.value: rapidyaml through 0.16.0 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ParseEngine::_add_annotation() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying YAML with excess anchors or tags. Attackers can submit YAML with consecutive anchors or tags to overflow the fixed two-element annotation array in release builds, corrupting stack memory and crashing the process.

cna.title: psqlODBC row cache overflow when a later FETCH changes the column count

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The driver rejects a column count that changes between fetches of the same cursor, and a keyset reply with fewer columns than the key fields.

workarounds.value: Set UseDeclareFetch=0, or connect only to servers authenticated with sslmode=verify-full or an equivalent GSS setting.

descriptions.value: psqlODBC sizes its row cache from the column count of a cursor's first result, but recomputes the column count from each later FETCH reply without checking that it matches. A server not trusted under current SSL settings can answer a later FETCH with more columns and make the driver write tuple records past the end of the heap allocation. A keyset reply with fewer columns than the key fields also underflows the unsigned field count. This is reachable with UseDeclareFetch enabled. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: ShortPixel Image Optimizer <= 6.6.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via CDN URL Rewriter

affected.product: ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF

descriptions.value: The ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the administrator to have enabled the 'Deliver WebP/AVIF images using the ShortPixel CDN' (useCDN) option, after which any unauthenticated visitor can submit a comment containing a crafted url() payload inside an allowed HTML construct such as <acronym title="...">, which WordPress comment kses preserves on save; the dangerous attribute-boundary breakout occurs only at render time inside the ob_start output-buffer rewriter, where kses does not apply.

cna.title: iubenda | All-in-one Compliance for GDPR / CCPA Cookie Consent + more <= 3.13.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via IUB-COOKIE-BLOCK Marker

affected.product: iubenda | All-in-one Compliance for GDPR / CCPA Cookie Consent + more

descriptions.value: The iubenda | All-in-one Compliance for GDPR / CCPA Cookie Consent + more plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 3.13.6. This is due to the way iubendaParser::parse_comments() re-processes HTML inside IUB-COOKIE-BLOCK markers through the bundled simple_html_dom parser after WordPress has already KSES-filtered the saved comment: simple_html_dom's remove_noise() stores <code> bodies under a deterministic key ('___noise___ 1000') and restore_noise() later substitutes any matching substring back into attribute values WITHOUT re-escaping, allowing a quote-breaking payload stashed in an allowed <code> element to be injected into an allowed <abbr title="___noise___ 1000"> attribute at render time. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, after an administrator approves the first (otherwise moderated) comment under WordPress's default comment_previously_approved setting.

cna.title: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in the ADM

credits.value: Jincheng Wang (@winmt) from Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

descriptions.value: CAPEC-591 Reflected XSS

A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. When the NAS is uninitialized, the endpoint accepts an unauthenticated sid query parameter and inserts its URL-decoded value into an inline JavaScript string without proper JavaScript-context encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when opened by a user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the ADM management origin. Successful exploitation may allow manipulation of the setup page and execution of same-origin requests in the victim's browser. The vulnerability is limited to the first-run initialization state.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

cna.title: An externally-controlled format string vulnerability exists in the Wireguard VPN Settings of the ADM

credits.value: Jincheng Wang (@winmt) from Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications
JU SEONG KIM 김주성(@http80) from Senior Researcher, Dronix (hans9407.kjs@gmail.com)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-135 Format String Injection

An externally-controlled format string vulnerability exists in the authenticated upload_wireguard action of settings/vpnupload.cgi in the ADM. The CGI takes an attacker-controlled WireGuard profile name, inserts it into a JSON object, serializes it, and passes the resulting formatted string directly to printf as the format argument without validation or escaping. An authenticated remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending format string specifiers, or leverage variadic read/write primitives within the non-PIE, non-Canary root CGI to potentially achieve arbitrary remote code execution with root privileges.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

affected.product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP and ABAP Platform (SAML2 Service Provider)

descriptions.value: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP and ABAP Platform does not perform sufficient verification of incoming authentication assertions under certain configurations. descriptions.value:
Web::Simple versions before 0.037 for Perl do not escape single quotes in HTML::Tags output.

cna.title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via decoded route parameters

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP requests to an upstream server under a configured prefix. In versions 9.0.0 through 11.6.5, when an application uses parameterized prefix and rewritePrefix options to pin clients to a fixed upstream path, the plugin substitutes URL-decoded route parameters into rewritePrefix without re-encoding them. A parameter value that encodes a path separator together with a fragment or query delimiter therefore decodes into real separators and delimiters that inject extra upstream path segments and strip the mandatory suffix the rewritePrefix was meant to enforce, without using any dot-dot traversal. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use this to reach upstream locations outside the intended prefix, leading to path-restriction bypass and, depending on the upstream, server-side request forgery or authorization bypass in the proxied service. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.6, and users should upgrade to 11.6.6 or later. There is no workaround other than upgrading.

cna.title: psqlODBC stack buffer overflow copying ctid and oid values for updatable cursors

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The driver rejects a keyset value that does not fit its buffer, and the query fails with SQLSTATE HY000.

workarounds.value: Set UpdatableCursors=0 in the connection string or DSN, so the driver does not add the keyset columns.

descriptions.value: For updatable cursors, which are enabled by default, psqlODBC adds hidden ctid and, for tables with OIDs, oid columns to the query. It copies each value into a 32-byte stack buffer using the length the server sent, without checking it against the buffer size, so a value of 32 bytes or more writes past the buffer. A server not trusted under current SSL settings can send such a value. So can any database user who can create a view with its own column named ctid that the application reads with an updatable cursor. Builds with _FORTIFY_SOURCE abort; other builds overwrite adjacent stack memory. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to Subresource Integrity bypass via whitespace in integrity metadata

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, fetch verifies Subresource Integrity metadata by splitting the integrity string on a single space, but the SRI grammar separates metadata by ASCII whitespace, which also includes the horizontal tab. An integrity value whose digest is preceded by a tab or other ASCII whitespace is parsed as a single unrecognized token and skipped, and when no recognized algorithm remains undici treats the integrity list as empty and accepts the response, so a server returning a body different from the pinned digest passes the check. An application that pins a response with a valid but whitespace-surrounded SRI value receives attacker-controlled bytes with no integrity error, and the attacker needs only to control the response body, not the integrity metadata. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, supply SRI integrity metadata without surrounding whitespace, using a single space to separate multiple digests.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user cache disclosure via same-origin redirect

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when the redirect interceptor and a shared response cache are used together, an authenticated request that is redirected to a same-origin target has the final response stored under the original request's cache key. That key omits the credential and carries no Vary header, so a later anonymous or different user can be served the first user's private response body. This results in cross-user disclosure of cached private responses. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later.

descriptions.value: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated account with only manage:users can use users.update to change the password of any local account, including the Root administrator and other accounts with manage:system, by omitting the optional groups argument, which is automatically allowed and bypasses destination-group authorization without checking the target's current privileges. cna.title: Integer Underflow Leads to Out-of-Bounds Read via Truncated Chunk in HDF5 Szip Filter

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in H5Z__filter_szip() in src/H5Zszip.c. When decoding a szip-compressed chunk, the function subtracts the 4-byte uncompressed-length header from the chunk length without first verifying that the chunk is at least 4 bytes long. A truncated or corrupted chunk shorter than the header causes the length calculation to wrap around to a very large value, and the decompressor reads far past the end of the chunk buffer. An attacker who can get a user or application to read a dataset from a crafted HDF5 file can cause a denial of service. Only builds with szip support (libaec or the szip library) are affected.

cna.title: Uninitialized Heap Memory Disclosure via Truncated Chunk in HDF5 Scale-Offset Filter

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an uninitialized memory read vulnerability in H5Z__filter_scaleoffset() in src/H5Zscaleoffset.c. The decode path validates reads against the allocated size of the chunk buffer rather than the number of bytes actually read from the file. Because H5D__chunk_lock() deliberately sizes filtered chunk buffers to the larger of the stored and unfiltered chunk sizes and fills only the stored bytes, a truncated chunk passes these bounds checks and is decompressed from the uninitialized remainder of the allocation. Unrelated heap contents are then returned to the caller as dataset data. Because the reads remain within the allocation, the issue is not detected by AddressSanitizer. An attacker who can get a user or application to read a dataset from a crafted HDF5 file can cause disclosure of process memory. This issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-19029.

cna.title: User Frontend <= 4.3.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation via post_content Parameter

affected.product: User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission

descriptions.value: The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.13 via the `post_content` parameter of the `submit_post()` function. The vulnerability exists because the protected-shortcode blocklist guard inspects the `sanitize_textarea_field()` copy of the submitted `post_content`, while the copy actually persisted to the database is processed through `wp_kses()`, whose `wp_kses_no_null()` step strips C0 control bytes — allowing an attacker to inject a single `\x01` byte inside the `[wpuf-registration]` tag name to defeat the `strpos()` blocklist check while the clean, functional shortcode is stored verbatim; `strip_shortcodes()` does not neutralize the stored shortcode either, because the Frontend container that registers it via `add_shortcode()` is only instantiated when `is_admin()` is false, and `admin-ajax` requests have `is_admin() === true`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject a `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` shortcode into a published post, causing a live Editor-role registration form to be rendered publicly on the frontend that any visitor — or the attacker themselves — can submit to mint a WordPress Editor account with an immediately active privileged session when the default `autologin_after_registration` setting is enabled.

The plugin appends a '.html' extension to the attacker-supplied path before reading it, so files with any other extension — including wp-config.php — are out of reach. cna.title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via percent-encoded backslash dot-segments

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP requests to an upstream server under a configured prefix. In versions 11.6.0 through 11.6.2, the destination validation normalizes literal backslashes before it percent-decodes the request path, so a path that encodes its backslashes and dot-segments survives the dot-segment check and is only turned into backslash and double-dot sequences after that check has passed. When the upstream resolves on a platform that treats a backslash as a path separator, the forwarded request walks out of the configured proxy prefix and reaches a sibling location on the upstream. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use this to retrieve upstream resources outside the intended prefix, so the impact is confidentiality only, and exploitation depends on the upstream's path handling. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.3, and users should upgrade to 11.6.3 or later. This is a follow-up to the earlier prefix-escape fix, which did not account for the encoded-backslash form.

credits.value: F5 acknowledges ruokeqx for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

workarounds.value:
Use one of the following options:

  *  Disable proxy_protocol v2; by setting proxy_protocol off; or using v1 with proxy_protocol on;
  *  Disable abbreviated SSL handshakes by setting both ssl_session_tickets off; and ssl_session_cache off;.

cna.title: frr: bgpd double free of peer-group Site-of-Origin when dynamic neighbors disconnect

credits.value: Nageswara Soma <nsoma@cisco.com> (not reported as security issue)

workarounds.value: Do not configure "neighbor <peer-group> soo" on a peer-group used by "bgp listen range". Instead, set the SoO extended community with an inbound route-map, or set "neighbor soo" on statically configured neighbors. Configuring a TCP-MD5 "password" on the peer-group limits the trigger to hosts that know the key.

descriptions.value: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.

descriptions.description: CWE-416 Use After Free: the peer-group's SoO pointer is left dangling after the first dynamic neighbor is deleted and is read by later neighbors and by the configuration writer

descriptions.value: An attacker who registers someone else's email address before that person first signs in with Google, or before they follow a confirmation link, ends up sharing that person's account: the attacker keeps signing in with the password they chose and sees and does whatever the victim can, in every organization the victim joins, at the victim's role. On an account linked to Google the victim cannot reset the password to lock the attacker out.

solutions.value: Upgrading does not undo links already made. Review the users rows that carry both a password_hash and a google_id; most are one person signing in both ways, but an account registered for someone else's address was usually created well before its first Google sign-in, so compare inserted_at with google_last_synced_at. For one its owner did not set up, set its google_id to NULL, delete its user_tokens rows to end its sessions and revoke its API tokens, and have the address's owner reset the password. An account taken through a confirmation link looks the same as one its owner set up; its owner can end anyone else's access by resetting the password, which ends every session and revokes every API token. Before upgrading, check how your instance lets people sign up: SIGN_UP_METHODS replaces OPEN_FOR_REGISTRATIONS, and instances that relied on Google sign-in to create accounts while registrations were off need SIGN_UP_METHODS=google.

Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an attacker who registers another person's email address to share that person's account once they sign in. NervesHub.Accounts.update_or_create_user_from_ueberauth/1 signs a Google user in to any account carrying the same email that is not yet linked to a Google account, links it and marks the email confirmed, without the account's owner ever having proved they own the address. NervesHubWeb.SessionController.confirm/2 likewise signs in whoever follows a confirmation link. An attacker registers the address from the sign-up form, changes their own account's email to it, or registers it as an organization admin from an invite link, and keeps the password; when the address's owner signs in with Google or follows the confirmation link, they land in that account.

The Google path also creates accounts with registrations closed and never checks Google's email_verified claim, and the API's password sign-in in NervesHubWeb.API.UserController issues tokens to accounts whose email was never confirmed. The attacker gains only what the victim is granted afterwards, and nothing on accounts whose owners never use either path.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.3.

With Google sign-in turned on and registrations open:

* Register an account with victim@example.com and a password you choose. Do not confirm it.
* The owner of victim@example.com signs in to NervesHub with Google for the first time. They are signed in to your account, and its email is now marked confirmed.
* An organization invites victim@example.com and the victim accepts while signed in.
* Sign in with victim@example.com and your password. You are a member of the organization at the role it gave the victim.

Without Google sign-in, as an admin of an organization:

* Invite victim@example.com, copy the invite link from the members page, and register from it with a password you choose.
* Try to sign in with victim@example.com and your password. NervesHub refuses, since the email is not confirmed, and emails victim@example.com a confirmation link.
* The victim follows the link and is signed in to your account. Keep using your session or sign in with your password.

descriptions.value: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). cna.title: Strapi Vulnerable to SQL Injection in Content Type Builder

descriptions.value: Strapi is an open source headless content management system. In versions on the 4.x branch prior to 4.26.1 and on the 5.x branch prior to 5.33.2, a database-query injection vulnerability existed in the Strapi Content-Type Builder write API. An authenticated administrator could inject arbitrary database statements through the `column.defaultTo` attribute when creating or modifying a content type. Setting `defaultTo` as a tuple `[value, { isRaw: true }]` caused the value to be passed directly into Knex's `db.connection.raw()` during schema migration without sanitization, allowing arbitrary statement execution at the database layer. Depending on the database engine, this enabled arbitrary file read via database utility functions, denial of service via forced server crash on schema-migration error, and on engines that permit external program execution, remote code execution against the database server. The patch in versions 4.26.1 and 5.33.2 addresses this by restricting all Content-Type Builder write APIs to development mode only. Production deployments running v5.33.2 or later return 404 for requests against `/content-type-builder/content-types` and related endpoints, removing the network-reachable attack surface entirely.

cna.title: ASN1_TYPE Type Confusion in the PKCS7_digest_from_attributes() function

descriptions.value:
Issue summary: A type confusion vulnerability exists in the signature
verification of signed PKCS#7 data where an ASN1_TYPE union member is
accessed without first validating the type, causing an invalid or NULL
pointer dereference when processing malformed PKCS#7 data.

Impact summary: An application performing signature verification of PKCS#7
data or calling directly the PKCS7_digest_from_attributes() function can be
caused to dereference an invalid or NULL pointer when reading, resulting in
a Denial of Service.

The function PKCS7_digest_from_attributes() accesses the message digest attribute
value without validating its type. When the type is not V_ASN1_OCTET_STRING,
this results in accessing invalid memory through the ASN1_TYPE union, causing
a crash.

Exploiting this vulnerability requires an attacker to provide a malformed
signed PKCS#7 to an application that verifies it. The impact of the
exploit is just a Denial of Service, the PKCS7 API is legacy and applications
should be using the CMS API instead. For these reasons the issue was
assessed as Low severity.

The FIPS modules in 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are not affected by this issue,
as the PKCS#7 parsing implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module
boundary.

OpenSSL 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3, 3.0, 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 are vulnerable to this issue.

cna.title: RIOT OS <= 2026.01-devel-317 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow in ethos Serial Frame Parser

descriptions.value: RIOT OS versions up to and including 2026.01-devel-317 contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the ethos utility due to missing bounds checking when processing incoming serial frame data. The vulnerability occurs in the _handle_char() function, where incoming frame bytes are appended to a fixed-size stack buffer without verifying that the current write index remains within bounds. An attacker capable of sending crafted serial or TCP-framed input can cause the current write index to exceed the buffer size, resulting in a write past the end of the stack buffer. This condition leads to memory corruption and application crash.

descriptions.value: A global buffer overflow flaw has been discovered in FreeRDP. This global-buffer-overflow was observed in FreeRDP's Base64 decoding path. The root cause appears to be implementation-defined char signedness: on Arm/AArch64 builds, plain char is treated as unsigned, so the guard c <= 0 can be optimized into a simple c != 0 check. As a result, non-ASCII bytes (e.g., 0x80-0xFF) may bypass the intended range restriction and be used as an index into a global lookup table, causing out-of-bounds access.

cna.title: FreeRDP has a global-buffer-overflow in crypto_base64_decode

descriptions.value: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol. Prior to 3.20.1, global-buffer-overflow was observed in FreeRDP's Base64 decoding path. The root cause appears to be implementation-defined char signedness: on Arm/AArch64 builds, plain char is treated as unsigned, so the guard c <= 0 can be optimized into a simple c != 0 check. As a result, non-ASCII bytes (e.g., 0x80-0xFF) may bypass the intended range restriction and be used as an index into a global lookup table, causing out-of-bounds access. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.20.1.

cna.title: RustCrypto SM2-PKE has Unchecked AffinePoint Decoding (unwrap) in decrypt()

descriptions.value: RustCrypto: Elliptic Curves is general purpose Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) support, including types and traits for representing various elliptic curve forms, scalars, points, and public/secret keys composed thereof. In versions 0.14.0-pre.0 and 0.14.0-rc.0, a denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the SM2 PKE decryption path where an invalid elliptic-curve point (C1) is decoded and the resulting value is unwrapped without checking. Specifically, AffinePoint::from_encoded_point(&encoded_c1) may return a None/CtOption::None when the supplied coordinates are syntactically valid but do not lie on the SM2 curve. The calling code previously used .unwrap(), causing a panic when presented with such input. This issue has been patched via commit 085b7be.

cna.title: Fast DDS DDSSQLFilter Recursive Parser Stack Exhaustion (Remote DoS)

descriptions.value: eprosima Fast DDS is a C++ implementation of the DDS (Data Distribution Service) standard of the OMG (Object Management Group). Prior to versions 2.6.12, 2.14.6, 3.2.4, and 3.4.3, Fast DDS’s implementation of SQL‑based content filtering (DDSSQLFilter) allows any participant in a DDS domain to remotely crash other Fast DDS participants by sending a single crafted SEDP `DATA` submessage whose `PID_CONTENT_FILTER_PROPERTY.filterExpression` contains a deeply nested filter expression. Versions 2.6.12, 2.14.6, 3.2.4, and 3.4.3 fix the issue.

cna.title: October CMS: Twig Sandbox Bypass via Collection Methods

descriptions.value: October is a Content Management System (CMS) and web platform. Versions prior to 3.7.13 and versions 4.0.0 through 4.1.4 contain a sandbox bypass vulnerability in the optional Twig safe mode feature (CMS_SAFE_MODE). Certain methods on the collect() helper were not properly restricted, allowing authenticated users with template editing permissions to bypass sandbox protections. Exploitation requires authenticated backend access with CMS template editing permissions and only affects installations with CMS_SAFE_MODE enabled (disabled by default). This issue has been fixed in versions 3.7.13 and 4.1.5. To workaround this issue, users can disable CMS_SAFE_MODE if untrusted template editing is not required, and restrict CMS template editing permissions to fully trusted administrators only.

cna.title: hermes's raw options logging may disclose secrets passed in via subcommand options argument

descriptions.value: hermes is an implementation of the HERMES workflow to automatize software publication with rich metadata. From 0.8.1 to before 0.9.1, hermes subcommands take arbitrary options under the -O argument. These have been logged in raw form. If users provide sensitive data such as API tokens (e.g., via hermes deposit -O invenio_rdm.auth_token SECRET), these are written to the log file in plain text, making them available to whoever can access the log file. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.9.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

cna.title: Kyverno Cross-Namespace Privilege Escalation via Policy apiCall

descriptions.value: Kyverno is a policy engine designed for cloud native platform engineering teams. Versions prior to 1.16.3 and 1.15.3 have a critical authorization boundary bypass in namespaced Kyverno Policy apiCall. The resolved `urlPath` is executed using the Kyverno admission controller ServiceAccount, with no enforcement that the request is limited to the policy’s namespace. As a result, any authenticated user with permission to create a namespaced Policy can cause Kyverno to perform Kubernetes API requests using Kyverno’s admission controller identity, targeting any API path allowed by that ServiceAccount’s RBAC. This breaks namespace isolation by enabling cross-namespace reads (for example, ConfigMaps and, where permitted, Secrets) and allows cluster-scoped or cross-namespace writes (for example, creating ClusterPolicies) by controlling the urlPath through context variable substitution. Versions 1.16.3 and 1.15.3 contain a patch for the vulnerability.

cna.title: DevToys Path Traversal (“Zip Slip”) Vulnerability in DevToys Extension Installation

descriptions.value: DevToys is a desktop app for developers. In versions from 2.0.0.0 to before 2.0.9.0, a path traversal vulnerability exists in the DevToys extension installation mechanism. When processing extension packages (NUPKG archives), DevToys does not sufficiently validate file paths contained within the archive. A malicious extension package could include crafted file entries such as ../../…/target-file, causing the extraction process to write files outside the intended extensions directory. This flaw enables an attacker to overwrite arbitrary files on the user’s system with the privileges of the DevToys process. Depending on the environment, this may lead to code execution, configuration tampering, or corruption of application or system files. This issue has been patched in version 2.0.9.0.

cna.title: nvme-tcp: fix NULL pointer dereferences in nvmet_tcp_build_pdu_iovec

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The vulnerable code is in the NVMe over TCP target receive path and is reachable by sending NVMe/TCP PDUs to the target TCP listener. A remote peer can send ICREQ followed by malformed H2C_DATA over the network.
AC:L - No race or hard-to-control state is required for the pre-CONNECT trigger; the attacker only needs to send a valid IC handshake and then an H2C_DATA PDU with coherent length fields. The required packet sequence is deterministic.
PR:N - The simplest trigger occurs after ICREQ/ICRESP but before CONNECT, before host NQN allow-list checks, controller creation, or DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication are reached. Thus an unauthenticated network peer can reach the vulnerable handler on a non-TLS or plaintext-accepted target port.
UI:N - Exploitation does not require any victim user action after the target service is listening. The attacker sends protocol messages directly to the NVMe/TCP target.
S:U - The impact is within the vulnerable kernel/target system’s own security authority. There is no VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-authority boundary change.
C:N - The bug is a NULL pointer dereference of uninitialized command buffers, not an out-of-bounds read or use-after-free. The investigated paths support a crash impact, not disclosure of kernel memory.
I:N - The dereferences are to NULL command buffer pointers and do not provide a practical arbitrary write or control-flow primitive. The fix and related history characterize the issue as invalid state leading to NULL dereference.
A:H - The vulnerable dereference occurs in kernel context and can produce an oops or panic in the nvmet-tcp workqueue path. Repeated unauthenticated network triggers can deny availability of the target system or service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme-tcp: fix NULL pointer dereferences in nvmet_tcp_build_pdu_iovec

Commit efa56305908b ("nvmet-tcp: Fix a kernel panic when host sends an invalid H2C PDU length")
added ttag bounds checking and data_offset
validation in nvmet_tcp_handle_h2c_data_pdu(), but it did not validate
whether the command's data structures (cmd->req.sg and cmd->iov) have
been properly initialized before processing H2C_DATA PDUs.

The nvmet_tcp_build_pdu_iovec() function dereferences these pointers
without NULL checks. This can be triggered by sending H2C_DATA PDU
immediately after the ICREQ/ICRESP handshake, before
sending a CONNECT command or NVMe write command.

Attack vectors that trigger NULL pointer dereferences:
1. H2C_DATA PDU sent before CONNECT → both pointers NULL
2. H2C_DATA PDU for READ command → cmd->req.sg allocated, cmd->iov NULL
3. H2C_DATA PDU for uninitialized command slot → both pointers NULL

The fix validates both cmd->req.sg and cmd->iov before calling
nvmet_tcp_build_pdu_iovec(). Both checks are required because:
- Uninitialized commands: both NULL
- READ commands: cmd->req.sg allocated, cmd->iov NULL
- WRITE commands: both allocated

descriptions.value: RustFS is a distributed object storage system built in Rust. In versions 1.0.0-alpha.13 through 1.0.0-alpha.78, a flawed `deny_only` short-circuit in RustFS IAM allows a restricted service account or STS credential to self-issue an unrestricted service account, inheriting the parent’s full privileges. cna.title: OpenHarness Improper Access Control via File Tools

descriptions.value: OpenHarness prior to commit 166fcfe contains an improper access control vulnerability in built-in file tools due to inconsistent parameter handling in permission enforcement, allowing attackers who can influence agent tool execution to read arbitrary local files outside the intended repository scope. Attackers can exploit the path parameter not being passed to the PermissionChecker in read_file, write_file, edit_file, and notebook_edit tools to bypass deny rules and access sensitive files such as configuration files, credentials, and SSH material, or create and overwrite files in restricted host paths in full_auto mode.

descriptions.value: CryptoLib provides a software-only solution using the CCSDS Space Data Link Security Protocol - Extended Procedures (SDLS-EP) to secure communications between a spacecraft running the core Flight System (cFS) and a ground station. Prior to version 1.4.3, when the KMC server returns a non-200 HTTP status code, cryptography_encrypt() and cryptography_decrypt() return immediately without freeing previously allocated buffers. Each failed request leaks approximately 467 bytes. Repeated failures (from a malicious server or network issues) can gradually exhaust memory. This issue has been patched in version 1.4.3.

cna.title: CVE-2026-22729: JSONPath Injection in Spring AI Vector Stores FilterExpressionConverter

descriptions.value:
A JSONPath injection vulnerability in Spring AI's AbstractFilterExpressionConverter allows authenticated users to bypass metadata-based access controls through crafted filter expressions. User-controlled input passed to FilterExpressionBuilder is concatenated into JSONPath queries without proper escaping, enabling attackers to inject arbitrary JSONPath logic and access unauthorized documents.

This vulnerability affects applications using vector stores that extend AbstractFilterExpressionConverter for multi-tenant isolation, role-based access control, or document filtering based on metadata.

The vulnerability occurs when user-supplied values in filter expressions are not escaped before being inserted into JSONPath queries. Special characters like ", ||, and && are passed through unescaped, allowing injection of arbitrary JSONPath logic that can alter the intended query semantics.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in devalue, a JavaScript library used for serializing values. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted input to the devalue.parse function. This can cause the application to consume excessive CPU time and memory, leading to a denial of service (DoS) condition. The root cause is an unchecked assumption during typed array hydration, where an ArrayBuffer is expected but not validated.

cna.title: devalue vulnerable to denial of service due to memory exhaustion in devalue.parse

descriptions.value: Svelte devalue is a JavaScript library that serializes values into strings when JSON.stringify isn't sufficient for the job. From 5.3.0 to 5.6.1, certain inputs can cause devalue.parse to consume excessive CPU time and/or memory, potentially leading to denial of service in systems that parse input from untrusted sources. This affects applications using devalue.parse on externally-supplied data. The root cause is the typed array hydration expecting an ArrayBuffer as input, but not checking the assumption before creating the typed array. This vulnerability is fixed in 5.6.2.

cna.title: LIBPNG has an integer truncation causing heap buffer over-read in png_image_write_*

descriptions.value: LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. From 1.6.26 to 1.6.53, there is an integer truncation in the libpng simplified write API functions png_write_image_16bit and png_write_image_8bit causes heap buffer over-read when the caller provides a negative row stride (for bottom-up image layouts) or a stride exceeding 65535 bytes. The bug was introduced in libpng 1.6.26 (October 2016) by casts added to silence compiler warnings on 16-bit systems. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.6.54.

cna.title: AutoGPT's API Keys and Secrets Logged in Plaintext in Stagehand Integration Blocks

descriptions.value: AutoGPT is a platform that allows users to create, deploy, and manage continuous artificial intelligence agents that automate complex workflows. Prior to autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.46, the AutoGPT platform's Stagehand integration blocks log API keys and authentication secrets in plaintext using logger.info() statements. This occurs in three separate block implementations (StagehandObserveBlock, StagehandActBlock, and StagehandExtractBlock) where the code explicitly calls api_key.get_secret_value() and logs the result. This issue has been patched in autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.46.

cna.title: sealed-secrets /v1/rotate can widen sealing scope to cluster-wide via attacker-controlled template annotations

descriptions.value:
Bitnami Sealed Secrets is vulnerable to a scope-widening attack during
the secret rotation (/v1/rotate) flow. The rotation handler derives the
sealing scope for the newly encrypted output from untrusted
spec.template.metadata.annotations present in the input SealedSecret.
By submitting a victim SealedSecret to the rotate endpoint with the
annotation sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/cluster-wide=true injected into the
template metadata, a remote attacker can obtain a rotated version of the
secret that is cluster-wide. This bypasses original "strict" or
"namespace-wide" constraints, allowing the attacker to retarget and unseal
the secret in any namespace or under any name to recover the plaintext
credentials.

descriptions.value: Capsule is a multi-tenancy and policy-based framework for Kubernetes. The Capsule Controller runs with cluster-admin privileges. Although the TenantResource RawItems processing logic forcibly sets the namespace, this is ineffective for cluster-scoped resources. Prior to version 0.13.0, tenant administrators can leverage the Controller's elevated privileges to create cluster-scoped resources (such as ClusterRole and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration) that they cannot create directly, achieving cross-tenant privilege escalation and cluster-level attacks. The attack vector has a few limiting factors. This attack requires Tenant Owner privileges and requires Capsule Controller running with cluster-admin privileges (default configuration). cna.title: Sandbox Escape via Host Error Prototype Chain in enclave-vm

descriptions.value: Enclave is a secure JavaScript sandbox designed for safe AI agent code execution. Prior to 2.7.0, there is a critical sandbox escape vulnerability in enclave-vm that allows untrusted, sandboxed JavaScript code to execute arbitrary code in the host Node.js runtime. When a tool invocation fails, enclave-vm exposes a host-side Error object to sandboxed code. This Error object retains its host realm prototype chain, which can be traversed to reach the host Function constructor. An attacker can intentionally trigger a host error, then climb the prototype chain. Using the host Function constructor, arbitrary JavaScript can be compiled and executed in the host context, fully bypassing the sandbox and granting access to sensitive resources such as process.env, filesystem, and network. This breaks enclave-vm’s core security guarantee of isolating untrusted code. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.7.0.

cna.title: vCluster Platform's Access Keys Allows Access Beyond Scope

descriptions.value: vCluster Platform provides a Kubernetes platform for managing virtual clusters, multi-tenancy, and cluster sharing. Prior to versions 4.6.0, 4.5.4, 4.4.2, and 4.3.10, when an access key is created with a limited scope, the scope can be bypassed to access resources outside of it. However, the user still cannot access resources beyond what is accessible to the owner of the access key. Versions 4.6.0, 4.5.4, 4.4.2, and 4.3.10 fix the vulnerability. Some other mitigations are available. Users can limit exposure by reviewing access keys which are scoped and ensuring any users with access to them have appropriate permissions set. Prior to 4.10.0, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability exists in an administrative API endpoint responsible for terminating all active video conferences on a single server. cna.title: RIOT OS <= 2026.01-devel-317 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow in tapslip6 Utility

descriptions.value: RIOT OS versions up to and including 2026.01-devel-317 contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the tapslip6 utility. The vulnerability is caused by unsafe string concatenation in the devopen() function, which constructs a device path using unbounded user-controlled input. The utility uses strcpy() and strcat() to concatenate the fixed prefix '/dev/' with a user-supplied device name provided via the -s command-line option without bounds checking. This allows an attacker to supply an excessively long device name and overflow a fixed-size stack buffer, leading to process crashes and memory corruption.

Preact has JSON VNode Injection issue

descriptions.value: Preact, a lightweight web development framework, JSON serialization protection to prevent Virtual DOM elements from being constructed from arbitrary JSON. A regression introduced in Preact 10.26.5 caused this protection to be softened. In applications where values from JSON payloads are assumed to be strings and passed unmodified to Preact as children, a specially-crafted JSON payload could be constructed that would be incorrectly treated as a valid VNode. When this chain of failures occurs it can result in HTML injection, which can allow arbitrary script execution if not mitigated by CSP or other means. Applications using affected Preact versions are vulnerable if they meet all of the following conditions: first, pass unmodified, unsanitized values from user-modifiable data sources (APIs, databases, local storage, etc.) directly into the render tree; second assume these values are strings but the data source could return actual JavaScript objects instead of JSON strings; and third, the data source either fails to perform type sanitization AND blindly stores/returns raw objects interchangeably with strings, OR is compromised (e.g., poisoned local storage, filesystem, or database). Versions 10.26.10, 10.27.3, and 10.28.2 patch the issue. The patch versions restore the previous strict equality checks that prevent JSON-parsed objects from being treated as valid VNodes. Other mitigations are available for those who cannot immediately upgrade. Validate input types, cast or validate network data, sanitize external data, and use Content Security Policy (CSP).

cna.title: idpf: Fix RSS LUT NULL ptr issue after soft reset

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

idpf: Fix RSS LUT NULL ptr issue after soft reset

During soft reset, the RSS LUT is freed and not restored unless the
interface is up. If an ethtool command that accesses the rss lut is
attempted immediately after reset, it will result in NULL ptr
dereference. Also, there is no need to reset the rss lut if the soft reset
does not involve queue count change.

After soft reset, set the RSS LUT to default values based on the updated
queue count only if the reset was a result of a queue count change and
the LUT was not configured by the user. In all other cases, don't touch
the LUT.

Steps to reproduce:

** Bring the interface down (if up)
ifconfig eth1 down

** update the queue count (eg., 27->20)
ethtool -L eth1 combined 20

** display the RSS LUT
ethtool -x eth1

cna.title: libceph: return the handler error from mon_handle_auth_done()

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The vulnerable path is reached by TCP msgr2 frames from a remote Ceph monitor or impersonating peer processed by the kernel Ceph messenger. A malicious or compromised monitor can deliver the crafted AUTH_DONE frame over the network.
AC:L - The attacker only needs to send an AUTH_DONE in the expected authentication state with secure mode and an auth payload that makes ceph_auth_handle_reply_done() fail. No race, heap grooming, or condition outside the attacker-controlled peer is required.
PR:N - The frame is processed during the authentication handshake before the monitor response has been accepted as valid. The attacker needs no privileges on the vulnerable host.
UI:N - In a configured Ceph client deployment, monitor authentication and reconnect handling occur automatically in kernel workqueue context. No additional victim action is required once the client is connecting to the monitor.
S:U - The impact is within the same kernel security authority as the vulnerable libceph client code. It does not cross a VM, sandbox, or separate authorization boundary.
C:N - The investigated failure path is a WARN followed by a NULL pointer dereference through uninitialized secure-mode crypto state. There is no evidence of an information disclosure primitive.
I:N - The bug does not provide an attacker-controlled write or control-flow corruption primitive. The observed and described impact is failure to stop session setup after an auth error, leading to a null dereference.
A:H - The secure-mode path can dereference a NULL crypto request in kernel context and produce an oops or panic depending on system policy. This is a high availability impact.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: return the handler error from mon_handle_auth_done()

Currently any error from ceph_auth_handle_reply_done() is propagated
via finish_auth() but isn't returned from mon_handle_auth_done().  This
results in higher layers learning that (despite the monitor considering
us to be successfully authenticated) something went wrong in the
authentication phase and reacting accordingly, but msgr2 still trying
to proceed with establishing the session in the background.  In the
case of secure mode this can trigger a WARN in setup_crypto() and later
lead to a NULL pointer dereference inside of prepare_auth_signature().

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting')

descriptions.value:
When the setting for saving requests to non-existent
pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its
redirect table, and the administration backend renders it without output
encoding in the form used to edit a redirect. An unauthenticated remote
attacker can store script code with a single request, which is executed in the
browser session of an administrator who opens the affected redirect,
allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges. The
setting is disabled by default in new installations but may still be
enabled in older ones.

cna.title: Iris Allows Arbitrary File Deletion via Mass Assignment in Datastore File Management

descriptions.value: Iris is a web collaborative platform that helps incident responders share technical details during investigations. Prior to 2.4.24, the DFIR-IRIS datastore file management system has a vulnerability where mass assignment of the file_local_name field combined with path trust in the delete operation enables authenticated users to delete arbitrary filesystem paths. The vulnerability manifests through a three-step attack chain: authenticated users upload a file to the datastore, update the file's file_local_name field to point to an arbitrary filesystem path through mass assignment, then trigger the delete operation which removes the target file without path validation. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.4.24.

cna.title: dcap-qvl has Missing Verification for QE Identity

descriptions.value: dcap-qvl implements the quote verification logic for DCAP (Data Center Attestation Primitives). A vulnerability present in versions prior to 0.3.9 involves a critical gap in the cryptographic verification process within the dcap-qvl. The library fetches QE Identity collateral (including qe_identity, qe_identity_signature, and qe_identity_issuer_chain) from the PCCS. However, it skips to verify the QE Identity signature against its certificate chain and does not enforce policy constraints on the QE Report. An attacker can forge the QE Identity data to whitelist a malicious or non-Intel Quoting Enclave. This allows the attacker to forge the QE and sign untrusted quotes that the verifier will accept as valid. Effectively, this bypasses the entire remote attestation security model, as the verifier can no longer trust the entity responsible for signing the quotes. All deployments utilizing the dcap-qvl library for SGX or TDX quote verification are affected. The vulnerability has been patched in dcap-qvl version 0.3.9. The fix implements the missing cryptographic verification for the QE Identity signature and enforces the required checks for MRSIGNER, ISVPRODID, and ISVSVN against the QE Report. Users of the `@phala/dcap-qvl-node` and `@phala/dcap-qvl-web` packages should switch to the pure JavaScript implementation, `@phala/dcap-qvl`. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability. Users must upgrade to the patched version to ensure that QE Identity collateral is properly verified.
